title: fix(sim): the wire gouge reading says how deep the kerf enters
body:
## What changed

- The wire kerf law reads a signed clearance (`dist::entry` in `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/dist.rs`).
- A move that stands in the product reads minus the distance from its deepest point to the product's boundary.
- The gouge depth is the kerf reach plus that distance.
- The closed-cut law (`passes::gouge_at`) and the open-run law (`kerf::gouge_at`) use it.
- The threading law and the open-end law keep the unsigned `clearance`. They need only "clear or not".
- The verdict does not change. Each move that gouged before still gouges, and the post stays blocked.

## Cause

`dist::clearance` returns 0 when a move stands in the product. The reading was then `need - 0`, the kerf offset. Thus each gouge with the wire centre inside the part said 0.162 mm, also for an entry of 2.8 mm.

## Tests

New file `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/depth_tests.rs`. The walls lean by 2.84 mm over 20 mm. The wire is cut at the Z0 offset. The depth is known in closed form.

- `a_punch_whose_walls_lean_out_says_the_wall_shift_as_the_depth`: 1.42 mm at Z10, deepest 2.84 mm at Z20. Red before the fix (read 0.162).
- `a_die_opening_that_narrows_says_the_corner_entry`: the issue's lofted opening (10.34 to 7.5). Move 1 reads 1.42 mm at Z10. The deepest reading is at the Z20 corner: `sqrt(2) * (2.84 - k) + k`. Red before the fix (read 0.162).
- `an_open_run_along_a_leaning_wall_says_the_wall_shift_as_the_depth`: the same readings on an open run.
- `a_kerf_that_only_grazes_the_part_still_reads_its_entry`: a wire centre outside the part reads `k - clearance`, as before. Green before and after.

Mutations:

- `kerf.rs` call site back to `clearance`: the open-run pin is red. Restored: green.
- `passes.rs` call site back to `clearance`: the punch and die pins are red. Restored: green.

Gate on head 5c56d217f, all green:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 7 steps, 0 failed (sim lib, app `solid_law_goldens`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_taper`, `wire_verify`).
- `cargo xtask gate test a_tessellated_loft --crate app --binary wire_verify_tol`: ok. This test parses the deepest reading.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No real lofted STEP part through MCP. The pins use synthetic square sections.
- The deepest point on a move is found by a walk of 33 points, then 33 points around the best one. The error is below 1/1024 of the move length. A move end is always read exactly.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3211-wire-gouge-depth.md`.

Changelog: The wire EDM gouge refusal now says how deep the kerf enters the part, not the kerf offset, when the wire stands inside the part.

Fixes #3211

title: fix(sim): judge a wire taper at the model's chord tolerance, refuse an undercut
body:
## What changed

- A constant-taper Wire Contour is judged under the model's chord tolerance. The tolerance is the importer's chord promise (0.005 mm). A model that records a coarser chord uses that chord. 4-axis cuts keep their stated tolerance (#1170).
- The report line and a gouge name "the model's chord tolerance" for such a cut. Stated tolerances keep the old words.
- A new undercut law (`sim/src/verify/wire/undercut.rs`) judges the last pass of a constant-taper cut. A move that cuts a drafted wall at one judged height must cut it at every height. If it stands off the wall past the tolerance at another height, the post is blocked with `wire undercut: the kerf of move N stands ... mm off the part ...`.
- The law skips a move on a vertical wall. A taper on a vertical wall is a stated relief, as in the #536 and #1164 fixtures.
- `WireJob` has a new field `taper_chord`. `WireFinding::Gouge` has a new field `chord`. `WireVerdict` has a new field `chord`. The test literals get `taper_chord: false`.

## Cause

The generator lays the tapered wire from the section at one height. The facets at the other heights stand off the true cone by up to their chord. The kerf law judged those facets with a tolerance of 0, so the true angle was refused. No law read a kerf that stands too far from the wall, so a wrong angle that leaves material passed.

## Tests

- New suite `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_chord.rs`. The fixture is a cone punch with a 128-gon top and a 64-gon base, each inside the chord promise. The base ring is turned half a step.
  - `a_meshed_cone_posts_at_its_true_angle_under_the_chord_tolerance`: red before the fix with `Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 2 enters the part by 0.0007 mm near X-3.499 Y-0.086 at Z0.001 (64 move(s) gouge)`. Green after.
  - `a_taper_past_the_wall_is_refused_as_an_undercut` (5.3 deg on a 5.194 deg wall): red before the fix (the program posted). Green after.
  - `a_taper_short_of_the_wall_still_gouges` (5.1 deg): a guard. Green before and after.
- Mutations, each red, then restored and green:
  - Tolerance 0 for a taper cut again: the true-angle pin and the undercut pin fail.
  - Undercut law not called: the undercut pin fails.
  - Vertical-wall guard removed: `wire_taper::a_tapered_punch_posts_its_golden_and_its_cl_shows_the_poses` fails.
- Suites run green: `camcraft-sim` lib `verify::wire` (20), and app `solid_law_goldens`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_fans`, `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_taper_chord`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol`, `edm_machine`, `mcp_edit_machine`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `setup_align_non_mill`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: exit 0, 107 steps, 0 failed. The plan has 626 steps, because the `posted_gates` edit reaches every app suite. The run did not reach all of them. I ran the wire suites above by name.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A real STEP import of the issue's EDM-T3 part. The pins use a synthetic mesh.
- A die (a conical hole). The law reads a die with the same product rule as the kerf law. No pin covers it.
- A model that records a coarser chord. The code reads `model_fidelity::chord_of`, but no pin covers it.
- A real EDM control.
- The optional part of the issue (read the taper angle from a picked wall) is not done.

## Overlaps

These open PRs change other lines of `wire_verdict` in `crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs`: #3219, #3205, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978. This PR changes only the `WireJob` literal lines there, and adds the new function `taper_chord`. The chord is read from the entities, not from the local `material`, which some of those PRs move. The PR is not stacked, because it touches the same file and a different part of the function. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3210-wire-taper-chord.md`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a tapered cut is judged against the model's chord tolerance, so a meshed cone posts at its true angle; a taper that does not follow a drafted wall is refused as an undercut.

Fixes #3210

title: fix(wire): accept the facet mitre of a meshed round in the corner check
body:
## What changed

- The new module `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/rounds.rs` finds the facet vertices of a meshed round.
- A vertex is a facet when it turns 30° or less. Its circle must have a radius of the kerf offset or more, and a chord sag of 0.02 mm or less. A neighbour must be a facet of the same circle.
- The cover law in `laws.rs` gives each facet vertex its exact mitre excess, `k (1 / cos(θ/2) - 1)`. The allowance fades linearly along each chord.
- All other vertices keep the strict `COVER_TOL` (2 µm). The refusal text does not change.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3208-wire-facet-rounds.md`.

## Cause

The model mesh draws an r0.25 fillet in four 22.5° chords. The wire path is the polygon offset of these chords. At each facet vertex, the path stands `k / cos(11.25°)` off the profile. For the 0.25 wire (`k` = 0.162 mm), this is 3.2 µm past the offset. `COVER_TOL` absorbs only about 15° facets. Thus the law refused a legal radius.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/facet_tests.rs`, wire 0.25 mm, gap 0.037 mm (`k` = 0.162 mm):

- `a_meshed_fillet_over_the_minimum_is_cut`: r0.25 in 4 and 3 facets, r0.5, r0.165 and r0.25 in 30 facets pass. On unchanged code it failed with the issue's text: "near X4.927 Y4.927 ... would leave 0.0032 mm standing".
- `a_meshed_fillet_under_the_minimum_and_a_sharp_corner_stay_refused`: r0.15, r0.1, r0.155 and a sharp square stay refused.
- `a_lone_kink_between_long_sides_stays_refused`: a single 22.5° kink stays refused.
- `a_drawn_polygon_with_facet_sized_turns_stays_refused`: a 16-sided R5 opening stays refused (sag guard).
- `a_short_notch_with_one_facet_sized_turn_stays_refused`: a short V notch stays refused (run guard).
- `a_round_in_facets_past_the_turn_cap_stays_refused`: an r0.25 octagon hole stays refused (turn cap).

Mutation results (each guard removed, then restored):

- `laws.rs` from upstream/main: `a_meshed_fillet_over_the_minimum_is_cut` red.
- No `r >= k`: `..._under_the_minimum_and_a_sharp_corner_stay_refused` red.
- No sag cap: `a_drawn_polygon_with_facet_sized_turns_stays_refused` red.
- No run check: `a_short_notch_with_one_facet_sized_turn_stays_refused` red.
- No turn cap: `a_round_in_facets_past_the_turn_cap_stays_refused` red.
- Restored: all 6 green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (motion lib, wire_fans, app golden_cl and all app wire suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. They must run before the PR is flagged ready.
- The issue's real STEP parts (EDM-T1..T3) did not run through MCP. The test uses a synthetic 10 mm square with the same corner spot.
- The path is still the offset of the chords. Against the true arc, it leaves the chord sag (about 5 µm for r0.25 in 22.5° chords) at mid-chord. This was already true before this change. The mesh resolution sets it.

## Overlaps

None. PR #3058 changes `wire_edm/open.rs` and `wire_edm/tabs.rs` only.

Changelog: The wire corner check accepts a meshed fillet at or above the minimum inside radius; it no longer refuses a legal r0.25 round because of its mesh chords.

Fixes #3208

title: fix(wire): stitch a plane's open runs and read a die face's opening as 4-axis profiles
body:
## What changed

- The 4-axis wire cut groups the picked open runs by plane. It stitches the runs of each plane with `stitch_open_runs`, the same stitcher that the 2-axis cuts use.
- When the runs of a plane close into one ring, that ring is the profile of the plane.
- Runs that do not close are refused by name. Runs that close into two or more rings are refused by name.
- On the die side, a face with one opening reads that opening as the profile.
- A face with two or more rings on the punch side is still refused. The text now says that the edge chains of one ring are stitched.
- The refusal for a curved wall patch now says what to pick: the top and bottom faces, or the edge chains of each outline.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3209-wire-4axis-stitched-profiles.md`.

## Cause

`wire_ruled::read` refused two or more open runs on one plane. `wire_ruled::profile` refused a face with more than one closed ring. Each refusal told the user to pick the other kind, so no pick reached the generator.

## Tests

All in `crates/app/tests/wire_fans.rs`:

- `stitched_planar_open_runs_generate_and_verify` (replaces `stitched_planar_open_runs_are_refused_by_name`): four top runs and a bottom face generate, and the wire verify has no problems.
- `stitched_runs_on_both_planes_generate_and_verify`: four runs on each plane generate and verify.
- `open_runs_that_do_not_close_are_refused_by_name`: three sides of a square give "3 open runs at Z24.000 ... do not close".
- `die_face_reads_its_one_hole_ring_and_verifies`: a round block with a tapered opening generates on the die side. The path stays inside the opening (reach below 8.5 mm, the outer ring is at 20 mm). The wire verify has no problems.
- `punch_face_with_an_opening_is_refused_by_name`: the same faces on the punch side are refused.

Red before the fix: the first four pins failed with the issue's own refusal texts. The punch pin failed on the old text.

Mutations:

- Old `wire_ruled.rs` put back: 5 pins red. Restored: green.
- Die-only guard relaxed to any side: `punch_face_with_an_opening_is_refused_by_name` red. Restored: green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (app lib, setup_align_non_mill, wire_4axis, wire_fans, wire_stamp, wire_verify_tol). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The owner's part `sam/sam_edm_part.step` and the EDM-T3 parts are not in the repository. The pins use synthetic meshes of the same kinds: a square outline as four runs, and a tapered opening in a block.
- The refusal for runs that close into two or more rings has no pin.
- The guard that refuses one ring plus a stray run on the same plane (`consumed.len() == n`) has no pin.
- The heavy lanes did not run.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `wire_ruled.rs` or `wire_fans.rs`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Wire 4-axis cuts accept an outline picked as several edge runs on each plane, and a die face's opening, as the upper and lower profiles.

Fixes #3209

title: feat(deburr): chord width, Constant Depth sizing and multi-pass breaks
body:
## What changed

- A 3D Deburr `width` is now the chamfer chord `w = 2 s sin(theta / 2)` across each edge. `theta` is the wedge angle of the edge. The setback `s` and the tip drop `s / tan(half-angle)` come from the wedge of each edge. `Chamfer2D.width` does not change.
- New `finishing3d::DeburrBreak` (in the new `deburr_size.rs`). `DeburrParams` and `OpParams::Deburr` each get one field, `sizing`, which holds:
  - `mode`: `ConstantWidth` (default) or `ConstantDepth` (`s = d / cos(theta / 2)`).
  - `depth`: the depth that Constant Depth holds on each edge.
  - `profile`: `Chamfer` (default) or `Round`.
  - `passes`: 1 to 100.
- Passes go from the outer pass to the final pass. Pass `k` of `n` cuts the setback `s * k / n`. Only the final break is declared as an `EdgeBreak`, and each pass stays above it.
- A Round profile refuses by name: "a Round break profile needs a ball-tipped cutter, and the chamfer mill is a sharp cone".
- Runs chain only edges that have the same drop. Thus each run keeps one depth and one declared break.
- Range limits: Constant Width sizes wedges from 30 degrees up. Constant Depth sizes wedges up to 150 degrees. The ride skips an edge outside the range, and a note gives the count.
- The project file goes from v74 to v75. A v74 Deburr `width` is multiplied by `sqrt(2)` at load. On a 90-degree edge the cut depth stays the same. The new keys are `break_mode`, `break_depth`, `break_profile` and `passes`. They are always written, and an absent key reads as one Constant Width chamfer pass. MCP gets the keys from `ParamsDto`.
- The record bound (`stock_sim_breaks::declared_width`) and the flute-length door now use the largest setback of the size law (`DeburrBreak::max_setback`).
- UI: the Deburr Geometry tab has new rows: Break mode, Break width or Break depth, Break profile, and Number of passes.
- The cache stamp digests the sizing only when it is not the default.

Note for the maintainer: the issue text says v61 to v62. Main was at v74, so this PR uses v74 to v75. The meaning of `width` changes for new operations and for MCP clients: the same number now cuts a smaller break (by `sqrt(2)` on a 90-degree edge). Project files are migrated. Decide if the title needs `!`. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1890-deburr-chord-width.md`.

## Cause

Before this PR, `width` was the radius of the cone at the edge's level. That is the setback on a horizontal face, not the chamfer width on the edge. There was no depth mode and no multi-pass mode.

## Tests

New pins:
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr_sizing.rs`:
  - `constant_width_holds_the_chord_on_a_120_and_a_90_degree_wedge`
  - `constant_depth_holds_the_depth_on_a_120_and_a_90_degree_wedge`
  - `passes_step_from_the_outer_break_to_the_final_one_inside_the_declared_break` (each cutting tip is on or above `EdgeBreak::floor_at`)
  - `a_round_profile_on_a_sharp_cone_refuses_by_name`
  - `the_size_law_names_the_wedges_it_reaches_and_its_bound`
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs`: `deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte` now passes `w = 2.0 * sqrt(2)`. On unchanged code it failed: the tip was at `-2.828427`, not `-2.0`.
- `crates/app/tests/deburr_chord_width.rs`:
  - `a_v74_deburr_width_steps_up_by_sqrt_2_and_a_current_file_does_not`
  - `constant_depth_in_two_passes_generates_inside_its_declared_break`
  - `a_round_profile_refuses_by_name_at_generate`
  - `zero_passes_or_no_depth_is_refused_at_the_command`
  - `the_sizing_edit_undoes_and_round_trips_in_the_file`
  - `the_record_bound_is_the_largest_setback_of_the_size_law`
  - `mcp_sets_the_break_mode_profile_and_passes`

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, pin red, then restored and green):
- Setback law back to `s = width`: the congruence pin and 6 other `deburr.rs` tests are red.
- Round refusal removed: `a_round_profile_on_a_sharp_cone_refuses_by_name` is red.
- One pass only: `passes_step_...` is red.

title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
Stacked on [#3205](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3205). The isolated comparison is [the inspection change above its parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10...d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0).

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification

Contributor head: `d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0`. Parent: `2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10`.

All eight scoped tests passed on the final head: two post tests, three MCP tests and three desktop tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for geometry, post, app and UI. The independent synthetic export preserved every directed edge, arc center and resource link. It wrote one start, one work and zero steps. The checks include:

- `agie_inspection_accepts_listed_chain_and_checks_mounted_travel_in_the_wcs`
- `saved_selected_opening_exports_zero_steps_through_the_desktop_action`
- `unassigned_inspection_opening_survives_undo_redo_and_project_reopen`
- `setup_post_inspection_fields_and_submit_fit_the_visible_panel`

The official full quick selector lists 1,039 steps. The reached heavy selector lists 253 steps. The release check is queued. This draft has a green targeted author check. The full selections have no pass result yet.

The desktop authoring and selection use a real undoable operation. The documented MCP reference was regenerated from the compiled CLI. The public selection returned by `list_features` can be passed directly to `create_agie_inspection`. A regression narrows the mount travel and reverses an axis. Each case refuses before file creation.

We used an offline VM running a copy of the actual Agie Classic Cut 2S control. The control opened native files produced by CAMCraft. We checked the program and ISO identities, nominal orientation, hole size and position, setup height, zero separation and zero working steps. Each work-level formal check blocked on undefined working technology. Each whole-piece check also flagged the low zero X/Y dimensions. Both control previews rendered the bound nominal profiles. An identical repeat import with the quality already present kept zero assigned working steps. Repeating an export to the same directory preserved the old files. No physical cut was made.

No model data, original job or simulator software is included. The public geometry tests are original synthetic cases. This inspection slice does not qualify a working erosion process, a physical slug restraint or an automatic cutting release. #3178 remains open for qualified curved die cutting. #3179 retains its physical process requirements.

## Desktop comparison

Both images use the same synthetic project and 750 by 830 pixel setup panel. The parent has the existing post controls. The new form shows the selected opening, wire and both start coordinates.

| Parent | This change |
| --- | --- |
| ![Parent setup Post panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-before.png) | ![Setup Post panel with the Agie inspection form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-after.png) |

title: feat(machine): record the installed control and tool-change procedure
body:
Part 1 of 2 for #3098. This change records which control a machine has. The post in #3182 will use these facts to select a supported dialect.

- A machine can state its control model, exact NC software release, installed options and tool-change procedure. An omitted option list means the options are unknown.
- The machine sheet, saved project and post interface retain these facts. Existing machine files can omit them.
- The Picomax 55 definition describes three-axis CNC operation with W fixed, NC software `340490-03` and manual tool changes. It leaves the absolute travel limits and installed software options unspecified.
- A machine definition that also contains conflicting script inputs gets a diagnostic. This preserves explicit restrictions such as `rigidTapping: false`.

### Evidence and outstanding checks

The target manual describes the retract in §7.4, p. 303 and the preset in §8.9, p. 492. The retract uses the active travel limit. Cycle 247 does not activate a preset in Test Run. [HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 manual for 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-neu/en/bhb.pdf)

The earlier Klartext prototype produced two programs for this installation. On the programming station running `606425 004 SP20`, both reached the end. The converter accepted 41 and 63 blocks. The station reached all three and five programmed stops. The physical machine still needs checks for the preset, quill position, retract clearance, drive state and coolant. This PR adds the machine data. The second PR supplies the writer and its golden programs.

### Verification

On `7afbcbaf6`, the quick gate passed all 378 steps. The test logs recorded 2,963 passes. The focused run covered 106 tests. These included the 11 existing Heidenhain DIN/ISO goldens. Clippy passed for the touched app and post libraries and the machine-controller tests.

The new tests cover installation data at both post entry points, missing or additional axes, and the distinction between unknown and empty option lists. They also cover an invalid mixed machine input and a Picomax project that is saved and opened again. The full heavy gate passed all 199 steps. It recorded 43 release test passes, including all six 3D finish bands. The gate classified the pre-existing expected failures under its existing rules.

Priority: P4, as on #3181.

Changelog: Machine definitions can record the installed control, NC software, options and tool-change procedure. The catalogue includes the Fehlmann Picomax 55 with an iTNC 530.

title: fix(geometry): import empty DXF layout and dictionary records
body:
## Change

Accept empty reserved model-space and paper-space definitions in the DXF BLOCKS section. Validate the record order and any supplied block record owner. Accept a bounded set of empty drawing dictionaries with validated entries and owner links. Report unsupported block geometry, object types and invalid references.

The importer previously required a literally empty BLOCKS section and refused OBJECTS. Those checks prevented a stock-face sketch from reaching the geometry reader even when these sections contained no drawing geometry.

The implementation follows the published DXF record structure. [Autodesk BLOCKS reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A3E4F1D3-79C9-489C-B7EC-3924DA7F25C9.htm) and [DICTIONARY reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-40B92C63-26F0-485B-A9C2-B349099B26D0.htm). It uses original synthetic tests. Actual block insertion and object geometry remain outside this change. See #1865.

## Verification

Exact contributor head: `636518a0a79016dbfb13c9d2c098faf3da2a17d1`. Base: `5e76e6a14b366c510858bbbf660c06ca013c34d4`.

The documented targeted quick check passed. All 44 tests passed in the five DXF suites. Strict Clippy passed for all geometry targets. Formatting on changed files and diff whitespace passed.

The new pins are:

- `empty_space_definitions_and_dictionary_forest_preserve_the_document`
- `layout_wrappers_refuse_geometry_external_content_and_broken_structure`
- `dictionary_entries_must_form_a_closed_acyclic_ownership_graph`
- `metadata_collections_obey_the_entity_limit`

An independent normal CLI check imported the synthetic control sketch with and without the metadata. Both produced identical feature JSON. The CLI refused an embedded block shape and a dangling dictionary. A separate normal import and project reopen retained stable chain identities.

The full quick gate passed all 1,038 steps on `636518a0a`, including strict Clippy. The reached heavy gate passed all 236 motion and application steps on the same revision. Both commands exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 5e76e6a14b366c510858bbbf660c06ca013c34d4
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 5e76e6a14b366c510858bbbf660c06ca013c34d4
```

A trial merge with upstream main at `a35c9cb81` completed without conflicts.

Effort: high. No escalation.

## Scope

Only DXF intake changes. The straight or curved Wire Contour planner and all machine posts retain their separate qualification requirements. No native controller job or physical cut is part of this parser check. No reference drawing or controller program is included.

Changelog: DXF stock-face import accepts validated empty layout definitions and drawing dictionaries.

title: ci(post-merge): one independent run per merge
body:
This PR needs the maintainer's decision. It changes a workflow in `.github/`. The runner tokens for more `camcraft-post-merge` runners come separately; this PR adds no secret and no repository variable.

## What changed

- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: the concurrency group is per commit, `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each push runs on a free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always finishes. The `gate` job does not change.
- The `report` job has its own concurrency group, `post-merge-report`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Its checkout uses `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body: `<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`.
  - The script reads the marker from the newest rolling issue, open or closed.
  - If this commit is an ancestor of the marker commit and is not the same commit, the script prints a notice and reports nothing (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
  - Otherwise it reports as before and writes the marker. A new red issue carries the marker in its body. A green run with no open issue writes the marker into the last closed issue.
  - If git cannot resolve a sha, the script reports as before.
- The red issue text now says that each run gates exactly one commit.
- `docs/decisions/3184-post-merge-per-commit.md` records the decision.

## Cause

One concurrency group for `main` let one run go at a time. A second push waited, and a third push cancelled the waiting run. A red run then covered several merges, and the breaking merge needed a bisect (#3111).

## Tests

Pins (all in xtask):
- `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_runs_each_commit_on_its_own`: the group is per commit and `cancel-in-progress` is false.
- `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_reports_one_at_a_time_with_full_history`: the report job has group `post-merge-report`, `cancel-in-progress: false` and `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `post_merge_report::order::*` (6 tests, unix only): the real script runs against a temporary git repository with two commits and a fake `gh` that records each call.
  - `an_older_green_run_never_closes_a_newer_red_issue`
  - `an_older_red_run_never_reopens_after_a_newer_green_run`
  - `a_newer_green_run_closes_the_issue_and_moves_the_marker`
  - `a_green_run_without_an_open_issue_records_its_commit`
  - `a_new_red_issue_carries_the_marker`
  - `the_same_commit_reports_again`

Mutation results:
- The upstream script with the new tests: 5 order tests red. The new script: 7 of 7 green.
- The upstream workflow: 2 of 2 concurrency tests red. The new workflow: 2 of 2 green.
- The guard without the "not the same commit" check: `the_same_commit_reports_again` red. Restored: green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (xtask unit tests). `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No real Actions run. The workflow change runs only after a merge to `main`.
- The real `gh` with `--jq`. The fake `gh` returns the final values directly.
- GitHub keeps at most one pending job in a concurrency group. If three report jobs wait at once, GitHub cancels the middle one, and that report is lost until the next run on `main`. The decision file records this limit.
- The `runners` skill (`.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md`) still says "A group of merges tests only the newest head". The edit of that file was refused in this session (a protected path). A follow-up must change that line.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Fixes #3184

title: fix(app): break a catalog-hint size tie by name, not file order
body:
## Cause

PR #3159 (f036dddad) added "Router ball nose 6 mm" to `assets/tools/catalog.json` before "BN-0600". `tool_gate::catalog_suggestion` selects the entry nearest 6 mm, then the smaller size. A full tie kept the first entry in file order. Thus the refusal for a ball-nose operation named 'Router ball nose 6 mm', and `the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry` (which expects 'BN-0600') failed on main. PR #3139 has no part in the failure.

## What changed

- `crates/app/src/operation/tool_gate.rs`: when the size is a full tie, the entry with the lower name wins (`then_with(|| na.cmp(nb))`). This is a deterministic rule, not a preference for one tool line. The hint does not change when the catalog file order changes. The taper kind had the same risk ("Router V-bit 60/90 deg 6 mm" come before "CM-0600-90"), and the rule covers it.
- New pin `a_size_tie_picks_by_name_not_file_order` in `crates/app/tests/tool_gate.rs`:
  - the pair "Router ball nose 6 mm" / "BN-0600" in the two file orders gives 'BN-0600';
  - the full catalog and the reversed catalog give 'BN-0600' (ball-nose), 'EM-0600-4FL' (end mill) and 'CM-0600-90' (taper).
- The assert of `the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry` does not change.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3170-catalog-hint-tie-by-name.md`.

## Readings (own worktree, head 3f945362a, CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12, -j 12)

- `cargo xtask gate test the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry --crate app --binary tool_gate --exact`: ok.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` says that the diff reaches the 199 `app` heavy lanes (each `app` change reaches them). They did not run. The change touches only the text of a refusal hint, not a toolpath or posted output. The PR is not ready until the reached heavy lanes run on the final head, or the coordinator decides otherwise.

title: fix(xtask): sweep superseded test-harness units at the end of a gate run
body:
## What changed

The cause is not "hundreds of hashes in one run". Readings in the build worktree `issue-917` (read only):

- The 634 `camcraft-app` unit directories are 627 distinct targets. Each integration test binary (about 620 suites) is one unit with its exe and pdb, about 100 MB. One set is about 64 GB.
- The growth comes from variants across trees and env. `camcraft-motion` has 747 units for 124 targets, `camcraft-post` 554 for 110, `camcraft-sim` 462 for 92. The variants differ in the profile hash (env before #3154) or in the dependency fingerprints (other `serde_core` feature sets). `Cargo.lock` and the manifests were the same at `8b4209215` and `cc04d7bcd`.
- Cargo never removes a superseded variant. So each change of env or feature resolution adds a full set.

The fix (`xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs`, called from the gate summary in `exec.rs`):

- At the end of each run (not a dry run), the gate removes a unit directory only when all of these are true:
  - it is under `target/{debug,release}/build/` of the gate's own root, and no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` / `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR` / `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR` is set;
  - its target fingerprint is `test-lib-`, `test-integration-test-` or `test-bin-`;
  - this run wrote a newer variant of the same target, and this variant is older than the run start.
- Libraries, binaries and build scripts are never removed. The newest variant is never removed.
- The sweep does nothing when a cargo lock of the profile directory is held, or when another process names `<root>/target` in its command line. A process list that cannot be read also stops the sweep.
- A failed delete is a warning line, not a gate failure.
- The summary prints the number of directories and the GB removed, or why the sweep did not run.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off` (or `0`) turns the sweep off.
- `seed::lock` is now `pub(crate)`, so that the sweep uses the same lock probe.
- The `gate` skill has one new paragraph.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3169-gate-unit-sweep.md` (cause, rule, why at the end in any outcome, why only test-harness units, what was dropped).

## Tests

`cargo test -p xtask`: 262 passed in the unit binary, plus the other xtask binaries green. `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Pinning tests in `xtask/src/unit_sweep_tests.rs`:

- `an_older_variant_of_a_target_built_in_this_run_is_removed_and_the_newest_survives`
- `two_runs_on_two_trees_leave_one_unit_for_each_target`
- `no_variant_written_in_this_run_means_nothing_is_removed`
- `a_non_test_unit_is_never_removed`
- `a_held_cargo_lock_or_a_live_process_removes_nothing`
- `superseded_never_lists_the_newest_variant`
- `the_process_check_finds_another_process_of_this_tree_only`
- `the_sweep_can_be_turned_off_and_reports_failed_deletes_as_warnings`
- `the_gate_summary_runs_the_sweep`

## Not exercised

- No real gate run with the sweep on a large target. The real process check (PowerShell `Get-CimInstance` on Windows, `ps` on Unix) ran in no test; the tests use a fake listing and a closure.
- macOS and Linux are not run.
- Fewer `camcraft-app` test binaries (the root of the size) is not in this PR. It is in the decision under "Dropped".

Heavy lanes: none reached (xtask only).

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Effort: high

Fixes #3169

- Five focused motion suites: 97 tests pass. The requested `center_cut_law`, `level_links`, and `machining2d` suites pass.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 235 steps pass in 37.4 minutes. The reached motion and app lanes pass.
- Heavy totals: 100 ordinary tests pass. No ordinary test fails or is ignored. The gate also accepts six expected failures.
- Heavy steps: one release build, 35 motion targets, 193 app targets, and six known-fail checks.
- `cargo clippy -j4 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, in 1 minute 25 seconds.

Review mutation checks:

- Disable the prior-feed check: the focused crossing pin fails. The broad pin reports the original six crossing pairs. Restore: all seven `center_cut_law` tests pass.
- Remove the closing rings: the square pin fails (two dives against four). The island pin fails (ten against fourteen).
- Force an infinite stay-down distance: the KeepDown pin fails.
- Restore the count and link mutations: all 80 tests in `machining2d` and `level_links` pass. The final tree is clean.

The other 24 motion targets and 173 app targets select no ordinary ignored test.
Known-fail checks remain separate from the 100 passing tests. Issue #1950 has two motion checks and one app check. Issue #2849 has three app checks. All six fail at their expected assertions, and the gate accepts them.

## What changed

- `pocket_avoid` (2D pocket with "Do not touch"): Zigzag and Auto levels now use `pocket_zigzag::rest_passes`. The rows stand 0.01 mm inside the level area. Then one closed ring follows each boundary loop: the wall, each island, and each keep-out edge.
- `machining3d::hsm::plan_level` (3D pocket levels, strategy Zigzag or Auto): the same plan.
- The rotary wrap (Rotary Offset) also reads `plan_level`, always with a seam. It keeps its rows. Its developed area ends at the seam, and a ring there cuts one seam line two times.
- `rest_passes` is now `pub(crate)`. `machining2d` re-exports it as `zigzag_ringed_passes` for `machining3d`.

## Cause

A Zigzag row touches a wall or an island only at its ends. A cusp stays between each two ends over the full depth. The plain 2D pocket closes its rows with rings after #3021. These two plans did not.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/pocket_wall_finish_levels.rs` (5 pins). Each pin measures the largest wall scallop at a level. Each pin also checks `verify::crossed_pairs`.

- `pocket3d_auto_levels_finish_the_boss_walls`

- avoid pocket: outer wall scallop 0.755 mm (0.919 mm with blended turns).
- 3D pocket: boss wall scallop 2.000 mm at level Z -5.

Mutation checks:

- `pocket_avoid.rs` put back: the 3 avoid pins fail, and the 2 3D pins pass.
- `hsm.rs` put back: the 2 3D pins fail, and the 3 avoid pins pass.
- Fix restored: 5 of 5 pass.

Expected test change: `operations.rs::multiaxis_rough_peels_the_same_ladder_and_poses_its_walls` had `posed <= 20`. The closing ring round the boss poses each ring chord (97 poses). The test now checks that each pose stays within the ball's reach (r 3, tolerance 0.5) of the boss. That is the intent of the old bound.

## Review fixes

1. A restart for a tool that is not center-cutting now stages its helix and checks it against prior feed moves. If it crosses, the restart tries a checked ramp along the pass. It refuses the operation if neither entry is clear.
   - Pins: `center_cut_law::a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting_never_plunges_into_a_pocket_between_passes` and `center_cut_law::a_closing_ring_restart_does_not_cross_the_rows_transition_ramp`. The focused pin requires a successful round pocket with a named ramp fallback and no crossings.
2. The square and island tests now describe the inset rows and their separate closing rings.
   - `machining2d::zigzag_fills_a_square_with_rows_and_a_closing_ring_per_level`: four dives, inset row Ys, and the row-plus-ring length.
   - `machining2d::zigzag_hops_over_islands_and_leaves_them_standing`: fourteen dives. The island distance and chord checks remain.
3. The KeepDown test now counts the rapid moves that successful planar links avoid. Its gap helper does not see those links.
   - Pin: `level_links::keep_down_pass_links_stay_at_depth_where_proved_and_say_where_not`. It compares the retract plan and a 0.001 mm stay-down limit. Verification and named-lift checks remain.

The decision record explains the changed counts and link assertions.


## Goldens moved

This review fix changes no golden file. The branch carries the NC and CL goldens and sample programs from #3130.

## Not exercised

- `pocket_avoid` blended turns have no crossing-law post as the plain pocket has (`hold_crossings`). The blended pin shows no crossing pair. If a crossing occurs, the post check blocks the program.
- Rings on the rotary wrap levels: not in this PR. Follow-up: #3168.

## Overlaps

- #3130: base of this stack (`pocket_zigzag::rest_passes`).
- #3108: touches `machining3d/hsm.rs`, function `rings_tag`. This PR changes `plan_level`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- `machining2d/mod.rs`: #3136, #3120, #3115, #3112, #3108, #3103, #3059, #2890, #2836, #2822 and #2714 add other lines. This PR adds one re-export line.

Fixes #3129

title: feat(import): state the STEP length unit, and ask for it when the file has none
body: ## What changed A STEP model import states the length unit that the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is never read in a guessed unit. - **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`, `solidcore_step.rs`, `solidcore_step_import.rs`): `read_step_assuming` and `import_step_model_assuming` take the caller's millimetres per unit. For a file whose contexts state no length unit, the unit is written into each representation context before the read. The tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are then in the same unit as the geometry. A file that states its own unit keeps it. A stated size outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. - **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`): `parse_open_assuming`. A file with no length unit and no caller unit is `StepError::MissingUnits`. `StepMesh` carries `length_units_mm` and `assumed_mm`. - **App**: - `ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`. - `ImportModel::within_in` and `from_bytes_in`, and the unit option on each import path: the file, the bytes, the sourced load and the cadmpeg conversion. - A unit for a file that is not STEP is refused by name before parsing, as a facet budget is. - The last import note names the unit: `length unit: in (stated by the file)`, `length unit: in (stated at import; the file states no length unit)`, or `... (stated by the file; the in stated at import is not used)`. - **MCP and script**: `import_model` takes `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). `cam.import` takes it as the fourth argument. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are regenerated. - **UI**: a refused unitless import opens the **Length unit** modal (`egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`), with the buttons Millimeters (mm), Inches (in) and Cancel. The answer goes through the command queue (`CommandKind::ResolveStepUnits`) and runs the same import again. The import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing. An import-as-fixture binding is kept for the second import. - **Docs**: `units-and-coordinates.md` (it said that a unitless STEP file "is kept as millimetres") and a new `troubleshooting.md` entry. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`. ## Screenshot The Length unit prompt for a STEP file that states no length unit (the status line under it says the same): ## Decisions (see the decision record) - The file's own unit wins over the caller's (the DXF import does the reverse, #1862). A STEP unit context is an exact statement of the CAD system. - The chosen unit is not recorded on the model. A linked-file re-import asks again. - Tool holders, fixtures and tool bodies from a unitless STEP file are refused by name, with no prompt. ## Pinning tests - `camcraft-kernel` `step_assumed_unit` (3): a unitless box reads 25.4² times the area in inches; the file's own unit wins; an out-of-range unit is refused by name. - `camcraft-app` `step_units_import` (5): the typed refusal; the inch and mm imports and their notes; the file's mm, in and m notes; a unit for an STL is refused; MCP `import_model` with no unit, a bad unit and `in`. - `camcraft-ui` lib `step_units_tests` (5): the question, the answer as one undoable import (inch is 25.4 times the mm width), Cancel, and no question for a file that states its unit. - `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::step_units_prompt` (4): the labels, no prompt without a question, a unit button, Cancel and Escape. - Updated, because each STEP import now ends with the unit note: `import_step_outward` (3 tests) and `import_step_closed_shell` `a_flipped_face_is_named_in_the_import_result_and_the_mcp_answer`. They assert the unit note in place of "no notes". No assertion is weaker. ## Gates Final head b5637db2b (the review fixes on 2649bb17e), Windows x86_64, without sccache: - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1033 steps, 1032 ok. The one red step is `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`, the CRLF defect #3119, which this PR does not touch. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (kernel and geometry on 2649bb17e; they did not change after it). - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): `kernel heavy` (17 steps), `motion heavy` (37 steps) and `app heavy` (198 steps), after one release build. 253 steps ok, 0 failed, 26.1 min. The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected. (The run on 2649bb17e also had 253 steps ok.) - Note: with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, two gate runs here failed with "can't find crate" (`num_enum`, then `flecs_ecs`) and the warning `ignoring -C extra-filename flag due to -o flag`. The runs without sccache are correct. This is a local cache matter, not this change. ## Review fixes (b5637db2b) - `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs`: the eight `load_open_within` calls in the `#[cfg(unix)]` module pass `None` for the new `units` argument. This module does not compile on Windows, so it is not in the Windows gates above. It needs a build on Linux or macOS. - `State::take_step_units`: each import start takes the chosen unit, whatever its file. A unit never waits for a later import of the same file. Pinned by `step_units_tests::a_chosen_unit_never_waits_for_a_later_import_of_the_same_file`. - `troubleshooting.md`: the answer is not kept; the next import, a linked file's re-import included, asks again. ## Not exercised - A unitless file from the cadmpeg converter was not tried. That path uses the same `parse_model_open_in`. - `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` were already over 400 lines. They grow by 2 and 7 lines. Changelog: A STEP import states the model's length unit, and a STEP file that states no unit is no longer read as millimetres: the desktop app asks for mm or inches, and MCP and scripts take `units` (#1874) Fixes #1874 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(setup): guided sheet job - stock, Z zero, through-cut allowance, XY zero, clamp clearance
body:
## Setup Settings screenshots

The same active milling setup is shown before and after the sheet-job checklist. These images render the shipping Settings page. The before capture removes only the new sheet-job group; the after capture shows the PR head.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Settings before the sheet-job checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/6364a66fe60717dc6792b7abdbc12b35039f0607/3165/settings-before.png) | ![Settings with the sheet-job checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/6364a66fe60717dc6792b7abdbc12b35039f0607/3165/settings-after.png) |

## What changed

- A new undoable command, `SetSheetJob` (`crates/app/src/commands/sheet_job.rs`). It runs the existing `SetStock` and `SetWcsOrigin` commands. It also writes a new setup field, `SetupDef::sheet_job`. One undo restores the stock, the WCS origin and the record.
- The checklist values are the sheet length (X), width (Y) and thickness, the Z zero (`top` or `spoilboard`), the XY zero (`front_left` by default, the other corners or `centre`), the through-cut allowance and the clamp clearance. All values are in mm.
- A new post gate clause, `sheet_job::program_problems` (`crates/app/src/sheet_job.rs`). It refuses the post by name in these cases:
  - a move goes below the sheet bottom minus the allowance;
  - a rapid that moves in XY is below the sheet top plus the clamp clearance;
  - the stock thickness or the WCS Z changed after the checklist ran.
- The project file saves the record as an additive key (no version step). The loader refuses a value that the command would refuse.
- A new MCP tool, `set_sheet_job`. `allowance` and `z_zero` are required, so an agent always states them. `{"clear": true}` removes the record only. `get_job` shows the job. The live gate classifies the tool as `LimitEdit`.
- A new UI group, "Sheet job", on the Settings page of a milling setup. The allowance row is always shown. A summary line gives the deepest Z. Apply queues one `SetSheetJob`. Apply on the page of an inactive setup is refused by name.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3070-sheet-job.md`.

## Cause

This is a new feature (P4, the maintainer asked for it). Hobby router users had to know the stock, height and WCS conventions themselves. Nothing stopped a through cut that went into the machine bed.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/mcp_sheet_job.rs`:
- `one_set_sheet_job_places_stock_and_zero_and_one_undo_puts_them_back`
- `a_through_cut_within_the_allowance_posts_from_the_stated_zero_and_past_it_is_refused`: the posted lowest Z is Z-10.5 with Z zero on the top and Z-0.5 with Z zero on the spoilboard. An allowance of 0.2 mm refuses the post.
- `a_rapid_across_below_the_clamp_plane_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_stock_or_zero_edited_after_the_checklist_holds_the_post`
- `the_sheet_job_survives_a_save_and_reload`: a save and reload keeps the record, and a corrupt allowance is refused at load.
- `bad_answers_are_refused_with_the_commands_words`

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_settings_page.rs`:
- `the_sheet_job_checklist_applies_one_undoable_step`
- `the_sheet_job_checklist_refuses_an_inactive_setup`

All pins fail on unchanged code, because the tool and the group do not exist there.

Mutation checks (each guard turned off, then restored):
- No gate line in `posting.rs`: the allowance, clamp and drift tests go red.
- Floor check off: the allowance test goes red.
- Clamp check off: the clamp test goes red.
- Z-zero drift check off: the drift test goes red.
- Loader check off: the save/reload test goes red.
- `invert` does not undo the steps: the undo test goes red.

Each restore made the suite green again (6/6, then UI 10/10).

Gate on the final head:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 472 steps, 0 failed (22.2 min). The schema change reaches every app and ui suite.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The first gate run had one expected red step, `mcp_doc_drift`, because a new tool must be in the docs. The second commit adds `set_sheet_job` to `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md`. It also writes `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` again with the generator command.

## Goldens moved

None. A setup without a sheet job posts the same as before.

## Not exercised

- A 5-axis or tilted-tool path on a sheet-job setup. The floor check reads the tool-tip Z of each move only.
- A WCS that is flipped or rotated after the checklist. The checklist sets an identity rotation, and the existing gates judge a later rotation.

## Overlaps

These files are shared with open PRs, but this PR changes different functions. Each hunk here is an appended line in a list or a match arm. Whichever PR merges second refreshes.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (#2714, #2836, #2951 and others): one new line in `verification_report_by`.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `mcp/mod.rs`, `mcp/job.rs` (#2716, #2773, #2920, #3033, #3058, #3061, #3103, #3108, #3158): one registration line each.
- `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`, `project/wire.rs` (#2716, #2920): one new field.
- `crates/app/src/schema.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, `lib.rs` (#2924, #3061, #3057, #3058): module or field lines.

The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_sheet_job` is not in this PR, so the PR changes no process file.

Changelog: Guided sheet job on a milling setup (Settings page and MCP `set_sheet_job`). It sets the sheet stock, Z zero at the sheet top or the spoilboard, XY zero and a stated through-cut allowance as one undo step. The post refuses a cut past the allowance or a rapid below the clamp clearance.

Effort: high

Fixes #3070

title: feat(catalog): a catalog case can expect a refusal
body:
Stacked on #3139 (merge #3139 first).

## What changed

- The `expect` field of `case.toml` takes `"post"` or `"refusal"`. Other values are refused by name.
- The 12 existing cases change to `expect = "post"`. #3139 held a free-text description there. The README of each case keeps that text.
- A refusal case has no `<case>.nc`. It has `refusal.txt`: the refusal lines that the script host records, one line each.
- The script of a refusal case saves the project, then runs the refused step without a catch. The script run ends with an error.
- The app tests `regenerates` and `rebuilds` read `expect`:
  - `regenerates` opens the saved project in the script host (`cam.load`, `cam.generate`, `cam.post`). It compares `ScriptOutcome::errors` with `refusal.txt`.
  - `rebuilds` runs `build.camscript` with `camcraft-cli`. It requires a failed exit, a saved project, no `.nc`, and the same lines on stderr.
  - The two tests also open the project and check that its model is embedded, with no file link.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check` accepts a refusal case without a `.nc` file. It runs the script and compares the refusal lines. A refusal case with a `.nc` file fails the layout check.
- `cargo xtask catalog` (rebuild) writes `refusal.txt` for a refusal case.
- New case `2d/drill-overfeed`: an 80 x 50 x 10 mm plate with two 6 mm holes. The Drill feeds at 400 mm/min, above the 115 mm/min of tool DR-0600. The post refuses it by the #2598 clause.
- The 2D operation guide lists the new case under Drill (generated block).
- The catalog README documents `expect` and `refusal.txt`.
- The script host law does not change.

Process change: yes
Effort: high. No escalation.

## Cause

The catalog tests and `--check` required a posted `.nc` for each case. A case could not show a refusal.

## Tests

New pins:

- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::regenerates`
- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::rebuilds`
- `catalog_check_verifies_refusal_case` (xtask integration)
- `catalog_expect_takes_post_or_refusal_only`
- `catalog_layout_accepts_a_refusal_case_without_nc`
- `catalog_layout_still_requires_nc_for_a_post_case`
- `refusal_lines_keep_the_cli_error_lines_without_the_prefix`
- `a_changed_refusal_text_fails_the_check`

Mutation results (each red, then green after the restore):

1. The app layout and dispatch as before (every case is a post case): the two case tests fail with `2d/drill-overfeed: missing drill-overfeed.nc`.
2. `refusal.txt` says 120 mm/min in place of 115: the two case tests fail with `refusal lines differ from refusal.txt`. `cargo xtask catalog --check` fails with the want/got lines.
3. The refusal case posts (feed lowered to 115 in the script and the project): `regenerates` fails with `the post was not refused`; `rebuilds` fails with `build.camscript ended without an error`.
4. `xtask/src/catalog.rs` from #3139: `catalog_check_verifies_refusal_case` fails with `missing drill-overfeed.nc`.
5. The `expect` value guard removed: `catalog_expect_takes_post_or_refusal_only` fails.
6. The "refusal case has a `.nc`" guard removed: `catalog_layout_accepts_a_refusal_case_without_nc` fails.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: xtask unit tests ok. `app:example_catalog`: 33 passed, 2 failed.
- The 2 failures are `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::regenerates` and `::rebuilds`: `did not finish within 60s`. The machine load average was 24-30.
- The same two tests passed alone: 54.6 s and 55.2 s of the 60 s budget. This change touches only the `expect` line of that case. Follow-up #3163 reports the small margin.
- `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/drill-overfeed --check` passed.
- `cargo test -p xtask catalog`: 23 unit tests and 6 integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets` (only the changed test target).
- The full `cargo xtask catalog --check` over all cases (the seed case and the refusal case ran).
- Screenshots and PDFs for the new case.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #3139: this PR changes the `expect` field that #3139 adds (`xtask/src/catalog_metadata.rs` `parse`, the 12 `case.toml` files and the tests that hold `expect` text). Merge #3139 first.
- #3136 changes `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_2d_slots.rs` and the slots case files. This PR does not change them.

Changelog: A catalog case can expect a refusal: `case.toml` `expect = "refusal"` compares the refusal lines with `refusal.txt`, and the new case 2d/drill-overfeed shows a refused post.

Fixes #2856

title: feat(ui): load machine and post files from the user's disk in the browser
body:
## What changed

The browser build now loads the user's own machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.

- **Load machine (.mch)** and **Load post (.cps)** are live in the browser. They open the browser file picker. A picked machine is mounted. A picked post is selected.
- The Machine page has a new button **Load folder (.mch, .cps)** in the browser build only. It opens `<input webkitdirectory multiple>`. It adds each `.mch` and `.cps` file of the folder to the session lists. It does not need the File System Access API.
- A drop with a `.mch` or `.cps` file goes to a new module `setup_file_drop`. One file is mounted or selected. Several files only join the lists. One status line counts the files that landed and names each refused file with its reason.
- On the desktop, one dropped `.mch` or `.cps` on disk goes to `LoadMachineFile` or `SelectPostFile` by its full path.
- A new app module `session_files` keeps each file by its bare name for the session, on the thread that loaded it. A file enters it only when it passes the checks of a file from disk: a machine must validate and parse, a post must compile and run.
- The readers of machine and post files consult the session store first, then the disk. So `LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile` and the MCP tools run unchanged. Each mount and post choice stays one undo step.
- Session machines show in the machine catalogue (`library::enumerate`). Session posts show in the post combo list.
- A saved project that names a session file which is not loaded again is refused by that name (#2319). There is no fallback.

## Cause

The browser build had no disk and no picker for these files. `browser_files::refusal` greyed Load machine and Load post with `NEEDS_PICKER`. The file drop took model files only. The readers of `PostRef::File` and the machine file read only from disk.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_setup_files.rs`:

- `a_dropped_mch_mounts_by_its_name_and_one_undo_takes_it_away`
- `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes`
- `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_malformed_pick_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `a_picked_folder_fills_both_lists_and_a_picked_file_mounts_or_selects`
- `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` (AccessKit label, role `Button`, enabled state for "Load machine (.mch)", "Load folder (.mch, .cps)" and "Load post (.cps)"; no folder button on the desktop)

Other tests:

- `session_files::tests::a_bad_file_is_refused_by_name_and_never_kept` (app unit test; also pins the refusal by name for a project that names a file that is not loaded).
- `setup_file_drop::tests::one_file_is_for_its_own_kind_in_any_case`.
- Updated for the new law: `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`.

Red before the fix (reduced pins on unchanged `upstream/main`):

- the drop pins failed with `drop refused: drop-2950-vmc.mch is not a model file (read: .stl, .obj, .step, .stp, .sc, .solidcraft)`;
- the button pin failed with `LoadMachineDialog runs the browser's picker` / `left: Some("Not available in the browser yet: ...")`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pins run, code restored):

- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` from upstream: `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` red.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` from upstream (drop route not called): the three drop pins red.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` from upstream (no session read at post time): `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes` red.
- `session_files::add_post` without its compile check: `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name` red.
- All pins green again after each restore.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 428 steps on the previous head. 427 passed. `ui suites: lib` failed in three machines-pane tests. The cause was a process-global store: the session machines of the new tests leaked into the machine list of tests on other threads.
- The fix makes the store thread-local. The browser runs on one thread.
- On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "app suites: lib" --only "ui suites: lib"` is green (ui lib 1385 passed, 0 failed). Only `crates/app/src/session_files.rs` changed between the two heads, plus one test comment and the decision file. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build. The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed on this machine, so the wasm-only code was not compiled. That code is: the folder input and batch read in `file_pick.rs`, the async drop read in `setup_file_drop.rs`, and the dialog openers in `state_picked.rs`. A reviewer with the target must run `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- A real browser. The tests use `State::browser_build` and in-memory drops as the stand-in.
- Persistence in IndexedDB. Not built. The decision file lists the options for the maintainer.

## Overlaps

- #3057 changes `file_drop::take_drop`. This PR does not change that function. It adds `setup_file_drop::take`, which `shell.rs` calls before `take_drop`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- Several open PRs touch `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in other functions. This PR changes only `script_of`, `resolve_cps` (one line each), the `LoadMachineDialog` / `SelectPostDialog` arms and one new `CommandKind` variant.

## MCP

No new MCP tool. The browser routes go through the existing `LoadMachineFile` and `SelectPostFile` commands, and the MCP machine and post tools read the session store through the same readers. `LoadSetupFolderDialog` is a browser-only picker. It changes no document state.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2950-browser-machine-post-files.md`.

title: feat(tools,app): cutting data for wood, MDF, plywood, acrylic and HDPE
body:
## What changed

- The cutting table has six new work materials: `softwood`, `hardwood`, `mdf`, `plywood`, `acrylic` and `hdpe`.
- Each new row has a cutting-speed window and a 10 mm chip load for HSS and carbide. Each row also has Kienzle constants.
- The new rows are appended. The table is indexed in `WorkMaterial::ALL` order. A project file stores the word, so old files read the same.
- New module `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` gives the router chip load by cutter diameter. The points are 3 mm 0.30, 6 mm 0.65, 10 mm 1.0 and 12 mm 1.15 of the 10 mm chip load. Below 3 mm the scale falls in proportion to the diameter. Above 12 mm it holds.
- `WorkMaterial::chip_scale(d)` selects the router curve for a router material. It selects the existing metal bands (`fz_scale`) for the other materials.
- `app::cutting::compute` uses `chip_scale`. On a router material, a V-bit (`ToolKind::Taper`) reads its chip load at half its diameter.
- The turning table has the same six rows, because it is also indexed in `ALL` order.
- The `camcraft-tools speeds` command, the MCP tool descriptions, the generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the `camcraft-mcp` skill list the new words.

The rpm clamp is the existing code in `compute`. It clamps to `spindle_min` and `spindle_max`. It then calculates the feed again at the clamped rpm, so the chip load stays the same. It names each clamp in `notes`. This PR does not change that code. The new tests pin it for a router spindle.

## Cause

The table had only aluminium, steels, cast iron, brass and POM. A router user who cut wood or plastics got no suggestion, or a suggestion from a metal row. The metal bands also give each cutter from 3 to 6 mm the same chip load. For wood, that is approximately two times too much for a 1/8 in cutter.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/cutting_router.rs`:

- `router_materials_have_words_and_round_trip`
- `each_router_material_matches_the_hand_calculation_on_a_6mm_end_mill`: S and F for each material against a hand calculation.
- `end_mill_v_bit_and_ball_nose_stay_inside_a_router_spindle`: end mills of 3, 6 and 12 mm, a V-bit and a ball nose, for each material and tool material, on a 10000-24000 rpm spindle.
- `a_v_bit_reads_its_chip_load_at_half_its_diameter`
- `a_router_spindle_clamps_both_ways_and_keeps_the_chip_load`: 3 mm softwood is held at 24000 rpm, with F 4320. 12 mm HSS acrylic is raised to 10000 rpm, with F 2875. Each clamp is named.

Unit tests in `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` pin the curve points, the ends and that the curve never falls.

Before the fix, the suite did not compile: the materials did not exist.

Mutations (each put back, each run, then restored):

- Old `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` (metal bands for all materials): 3 tests red.
- No half-diameter V-bit reading: `a_v_bit_reads_its_chip_load_at_half_its_diameter` red.
- `chip_scale` always returns `fz_scale`: 3 tests red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final head (24 steps). The first run had one expected red, `mcp_doc_drift`, because the MCP description changed. I generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` again, and the suite is green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- material cutting` is green (7 tests), because the UI iterates `WorkMaterial::ALL`.

## Goldens moved

None. The metal rows use the same expression as before, so their S and F do not change.

## Not exercised

- I did not start the GUI. The material lists in the UI come from `WorkMaterial::ALL`, and their unit tests are green.
- The turning rows for wood and plastics have only the table-order test. No lathe test uses them.
- The numbers are our own conservative values at the low side of public woodworking and plastics ranges. A human must still check them against a real router cut.

## Overlaps

- #3151 changes `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` in `feed_mut`. This PR changes `compute` in the same file. The functions are different. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/3068-router-materials.md`.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: Cutting data for softwood, hardwood, MDF, plywood, acrylic and HDPE, with the chip load by cutter diameter and the router spindle clamp.

Fixes #3068

title: feat(ui): show the operator side at the work envelope
body:
## What changed

The viewport now shows the operator side of the work envelope. An arrow starts at the lower edge of the operator-side face. The arrow points out of the envelope, toward the operator. The text "Operator side" is at the tip of the arrow.

- `camcraft-post`: a machine file can state `general.operator_side`. The words are `"-X"`, `"+X"`, `"-Y"` and `"+Y"`. The word names the world axis that points from the envelope to the operator.
  - The field is optional. Old machine files and old projects load without a change.
  - A wrong word refuses the file by name. A wrong word never reads as the default.
  - `OperatorSide::default_for` gives the default of each machine kind: `+Y` for a lathe, `-Y` (the front) for each other kind.
- `camcraft-ui`: `operator_side.rs` builds the arrow when its input changes (the placed envelope and the side). Each other frame reads the kept arrow. The text is screen text, so it stays readable when the view turns.
- The View door has a new box, "Show operator side". It is view state: on by default, no command, not saved. It is disabled while the work envelope is off.
- The arrow and the text use the envelope colour. They are outside the envelope, so they do not cover the part or the toolpath.
- Docs: `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the machine file grammar) and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md` (the defaults for each kind).

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for. The viewport did not show from which side the operator looks into the work envelope.

## Before and after screenshots

Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted and the work envelope shown. The camera looks from the front. "Before" is the same scene with the new box off. With the box off, the scene is the same as on `upstream/main`.

|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-after.png) |

The screenshots are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. A temporary collector made them. The collector is not in this branch.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/post/tests/operator_side.rs`:

- `an_old_file_without_the_field_loads_and_takes_the_default_of_its_kind` (also loads each library `.mch` file)

- `a_file_that_names_a_side_keeps_it_over_the_default`
- `a_wrong_word_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `a_stored_machine_without_the_field_still_reads_and_a_stated_side_round_trips`

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/operator_side.rs`:

- `a_mill_shows_the_arrow_and_the_text_on_its_default_side`
- `each_machine_kind_shows_the_arrow_on_its_default_side`
- `a_lathe_shows_the_arrow_on_the_viewer_side_of_the_turning_plane`
- `a_machine_that_names_a_side_moves_the_arrow_to_it` (also through the file text)
- `no_envelope_means_no_arrow_and_no_text`
- `the_switch_hides_and_shows_the_arrow_and_the_text_as_view_state`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_arrow_and_a_changed_input_builds_one` (the frame-cost counter test)

The pins do not compile on `upstream/main`, because the types are new. Mutation checks, each restored after the run:

1. The parser does not read `general.operator_side`: 2 post pins go red.
2. The scene draws the envelope without the arrow: 3 UI pins go red.
3. The cache builds the arrow again on each frame: the counter pin goes red.
4. The draw ignores the "Show operator side" box: the switch pin goes red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 92 steps. 91 passed. The `ui suites: lib` step stopped with SIGSEGV (signal 11) in the middle of the run; no test reported a failure. The re-run of that step alone (`--failed`) passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The shared sccache did not answer, so the gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

title: fix(xtask): pin the env that enters the cargo unit hash for gate steps
body:
## What changed

Cargo 1.100 puts each workspace unit in its own directory, `target/<profile>/build/<package>/<hash>/`. The hash covers the profile of the unit. Agents ran gates in the shared build worktree with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and with the default (incremental on). `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` sets `profile.incremental`. Thus each run with the other value gave all of about 600 `camcraft-app` units a new directory (about 190 MB each). Cargo does not remove the old directories.

- New `xtask/src/unit_env.rs`: each cargo call of a gate gets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`. The gate removes the caller's `CARGO_PROFILE_*` and `CARGO_BUILD_INCREMENTAL` variables.
- `direct::cargo` (the one place where a gate step starts cargo) and the three catalog cargo calls apply the pin.
- At the start, the gate prints the pin, each removed variable, and a note when `RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS` is set.
- The summary prints the number of unit directories that the run added.
- The `gate` skill tells about the pin. `docs/decisions/3150-gate-unit-env.md` records the cause and the choice (incremental off, because sccache cannot cache incremental units and the disk is the defect).

## Readings (shared build worktree issue-917, 2026-11-21)

- The manifests, `Cargo.lock` and `.cargo/config.toml` were the same at the last six gated heads. But the `profile` fingerprint hash of one test unit had 3 values over 5 runs. Third-party units did not change.
- After the fix, `cargo xtask gate test flat_volume_has_finite_width_depth_and_segment_ends --crate cl` ran two times: caller `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unset gave `unit directories: 5152, none added`; caller `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1` gave `unit directories: 5152, none added`.
- A plain `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 cargo test -p camcraft-cl --no-run` selected the other unit hash of `camcraft-kernel` (`573773ead6d4af3d`, an incremental variant). This confirms the cause.

## Pinning tests (`cargo test -p xtask`: 240 passed)

- `unit_env::tests::every_gate_cargo_call_gets_the_same_unit_env`
- `unit_env::tests::direct_cargo_steps_apply_the_unit_env`
- `unit_env::tests::batch_steps_share_the_flags_that_enter_the_unit_hash`
- `unit_env::tests::profile_variables_are_removed_and_others_kept`
- `unit_env::tests::notes_name_the_pin_and_each_removed_or_noted_variable`
- `unit_env::tests::units_count_nested_unit_directories_only`

## Not exercised

- A full quick or batch gate two times on the same tree. The probe used one `gate test` step.
- The old unit directories are not removed. The first gate run after the merge can add one more `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` variant where none is present. The decision file says why there is no prune.
- No heavy lane: the diff touches only `xtask/`, `.claude/skills/gate/` and `docs/decisions/`.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: none

Fixes #3150
