title: feat(2d): V-Carve operation - depth from the region width along the medial axis
body:
## What changed

- A new 2D operation, **V-Carve** (kind tag 44). A V-bit carves a closed region. The tip follows the medial axis. At each point the depth is where the cone touches the two walls. A maximum depth (`Top Z - Bottom Z`) limits the cut.
- Motion kernel: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/vcarve.rs`, `vcarve_axis.rs`, `vcarve_walk.rs`.
  - The tip positions come from the largest inscribed circle at each sampled boundary point. The centre of that circle is a point of the medial axis.
  - The cone keeps a wall allowance of 0.01 mm. The kernel checks each straight feed move against the outline before it writes the move. A move that fails becomes a retract and a new plunge.
  - A branch into a corner that turns less than 20 degrees is not ridden. A tessellated circle is one dip, not a star.
  - Deep carves step down. An optional flat-clearing pass uses offset rings of the same V-bit inside the wall pass.
  - The cone height also limits the depth. The path carries a note when it does.
- App: the `VCarve` kind row, the generator arm, the seed, heights, the mark depth law (`DepthLaw::Mark`), the project-file arm `VCarve` (appended, no version step), posting and the setup sheet.
- Sim: a new `Mode::Carve`. It has the stand-downs of `Mode::Engrave`, and the crossing law is off. The walk rides each axis branch from its two walls, so the two rides lie on one another by design.
- UI: a V-Carve parameter page and an original icon (`assets/ui/op-v-carve.png`, `.svg`).
- MCP: the generic `add_operation` tool takes the kind `V-Carve`. `list_operation_types` lists the kind and its fields. No new MCP tool is necessary.
- The V-bit is the existing `Taper` tool kind. The included angle is the tool's `tip_angle`.

## Sources (literature)

The algorithm is written from these published sources. The module heads name them.

- H. Blum, "A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape", 1967 (the medial axis transform).
- H. I. Choi, S. W. Choi, H. P. Moon, "Mathematical theory of medial axis transform", Pacific J. Math., 1997.
- J. Ma, S. W. Bae, S. Choi, "3D medial axis point approximation using nearest neighbors and the normal field", The Visual Computer, 2012 (the tangent-circle shrink).
- M. Foskey, M. C. Lin, D. Manocha, "Efficient computation of a simplified medial axis", 2003 (the separation angle).
- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991 (the floor rings).
- The cone law `depth = radius / tan(angle / 2)` is machine-tool handbook geometry.

The session had no web access, so no Perplexity search ran. camlib was a feature list only. No code or output of another program was read.

## Cause

There was no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth only.

## Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/v_carve.rs` (11 tests):
  - `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region`: sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline.
  - `the_depth_follows_the_width_of_the_region`, `a_sharp_corner_rises_to_the_surface`, `a_stroke_is_cut_in_one_engagement`, `a_tessellated_circle_is_one_dip_not_a_star`, `the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut`, `flat_clearing_removes_the_floor_the_cone_cannot_reach`, `a_deep_carve_steps_down`, `a_cone_shorter_than_the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut_and_says_so`.
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`: angle, diameter, maximum depth, stepdown, feed, clearance, retract, stepover, non-finite numbers, an empty region.
  - `degenerate_regions_give_a_clean_answer`: a fuzz set of 45 regions (zero width, a 1 micron sliver, a bow tie, a spike, far from the origin, 40 seeded random polygons), with and without flat clearing. Each gives a clean error or a path whose cone stays inside.
- `crates/app/tests/v_carve_op.rs` (7 tests):
  - `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted`: the letter L generates, the program sim finds 0 gouge cells, and it posts.
  - `the_letter_matches_its_golden_cl_file`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/v_carve_letter_l.cl`.
  - `the_operation_is_undone_and_done_again`, `a_tool_that_is_not_a_v_bit_is_refused_by_name`, `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_a_gouge_that_holds_the_post`, `a_saved_v_carve_opens_with_its_numbers`, `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone`.
- Red before the change: yes. The pins do not compile on `main`, because the kind and `v_carve` do not exist there.

### Mutation checks

- `link_ok` in `vcarve_walk.rs` always returns true: `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region` is red. Restored: green.
- `VCarve` removed from the mark law (`mark_law.rs`): `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted` and `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone` are red. Restored: green.
- `Mode::Carve` with the crossing law on: the letter L is refused (checked in the earlier session, see the decision record).
- `OpType::VCarve` declared after `Engrave` (its old place): `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` (the registry row law) and 13 more app and ui steps are red. At the end of the enum: green. The held work had this defect; this PR fixes it.

### Kind-table pins that take the new kind

- `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input`: the registry count is 45.
- `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`: the lathe refuses 32 kinds (was 31).
- `operation::types::tilt_basis::tests::the_tilt_slot_covers_each_kind_whose_file_shape_has_a_tilt`: `tilt_slot` now covers `VCarve` (code change in `tilt_basis.rs`; main's #2599 added the slot after the held work).
- `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`: `VCarve` is refused on a reduced model, as `Engrave` is.
- `ribbon::the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`: `SinkerSideBurn` keeps 43, `VCarve` is the tail at 44.

## Goldens moved

- One new golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/v_carve_letter_l.cl`.
- After the merge of `main`, its `START` line changed from `0 0 25000` to `6000 -3000 25000`. The cause is main's #2901: the opening rapid now starts over its own entry point. No move line changed.
- No existing golden changed.

title: fix(2d): rest pass keeps corner reliefs on the rest center boundary
body:
## What changed

- `rest_pocket_with_relief` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs`) keeps a planned corner relief when its start is in the rest center area grown by 0.01 mm (`RELIEF_START_TOL`).
- Each relief that the rest pass does not keep now gives a toolpath note: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: the rest area does not reach that corner`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3146-rest-relief-boundary.md`.

## Cause

The old filter was `.filter(|r| plan.center.contains(r.start))`. Each relief start is a vertex of the pocket's own center area. Where the rest area touches a corner, that vertex is on the boundary of the rest center area. `Region::contains` on a boundary point gives `true` or `false` by rounding. On a sharp 30 x 30 mm pocket, the rest pass cut 1 of 4 dogbones and gave no note.

The start stays a legal tool position. It is always on the plain pocket's own center area, so the tolerance cannot move the tool past a wall.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`:

- `rest_pass_cuts_all_four_dogbones_of_a_sharp_square_pocket`: the 30 x 30 mm pocket, 6 mm tool, previous tool 16 mm, `CornerReliefKind::Dogbone`. Each of the 4 dogbone ends is cut at the floor, for Waterline, OffsetRings and Zigzag. No relief note.
  - Red before the fix: `Waterline: rest pass missed dogbone ends [(27.88, 27.88), (2.12, 27.88), (27.88, 2.12)]`.
- `rest_pass_notes_a_forced_relief_the_rest_area_does_not_reach`: an override forces a dogbone on a 176 deg corner. The previous tool leaves only a film there, so the rest area does not reach it. The pass does not cut it, and a note names it.

Mutation checks:

- Old `rest2d.rs` from `upstream/main`: both pins red.
- The fix with a bare `plan.center.contains` (no tolerance): the count pin red, at line 72.
- Fix restored: both pins green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (motion lib, `rest_corner_relief`, `rest_zigzag`, `rest2d`, app `rest_pocket`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Heavy verification

The required motion and app heavy checks passed on unchanged head `50dbc2f0c9da14902afe3c1fe7ad5111ab2ca621`.
The base reference at the start was `c2423f1703f706bb3a6a9e98bd206fd1b96b5bd0`.
The diff used merge base `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`.

The local cache stalled at first. These completed commands disabled it:

```sh
CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER='' cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main
CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER='' cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings
CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER='' cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main
```

- Quick: all 6 steps passed. Motion unit tests: 490 passed, 10 ignored. The two `rest_corner_relief` pins passed.
- Clippy: passed with no warning from the touched crate.
- Heavy: all 236 steps passed in 89.2 minutes. No unexpected test failed. The six known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
- Motion heavy: 37 steps passed, with 57 tests passed and two expected known failures.
- App heavy: 198 steps passed, with 43 tests passed and four expected known failures.
- `rotary_field_parity`: all 6 tests passed in 533.80 seconds. The previous review stopped during this target.
- All 76 steps after that target passed. `shared_face_bodies_finish` passed all 6 tests in 1630.77 seconds.

No source, test, or golden changed. The accepted mutation evidence above still applies to this same head.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

title: fix(app): read a 3+2 plane and a cross drill through every table pose a post can leave
body:
## What changed

The Fanuc-style post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the move with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`, `onRapid`). On a machine whose table tilts the work, the X/Y traverse of a 3+2 plane or a cross drill then runs at the pose that the previous program left. The #2987 law reads these operations only at their own pose.

- `first_traverse_posed::posed_kind`: the posed law of #3084 now also reads each kind that carries a `Tilt` (the 3+2 planes) and the cross drill.
- `table_top` / `table_stays`: when every tilting rotary turns the work, the machine table is read fixed where it stands. When a head tilts, the #2987 table law reads it.
- **The post's declared order.** `tormach.cps` turns A at the safe Z (`G53 G0 Z`, then `G0 A`) before each section's first X/Y traverse. A post now declares that order with the manifest flag `rotariesBeforeTraverse = true` (`post::dialect::turns_rotaries_first`; the same pattern as `liveTooling` and `wcsRotation`).
  - `tormach.cps` declares it.
  - When the setup's post declares it, the posed law does not read the operation (for every posed kind, the #3084 kinds included). The #2987 law reads it at its own pose.
  - Every other post, a user's script without the flag, and a script that does not load read the strict way.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3100-table-tilt-first-traverse.md`.

## Coordinator decisions (recorded in the decision file)

1. The table is read fixed where it stands, not swept.
2. A test fixture change in `first_traverse_table.rs`. The test `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` sets the WCS origin to zero for `Rig::Work`. It now expects the verdict of the block corner on its sphere (29.584) at 20, and a pass at 30.
3. The cross drill: the one shipped mill-turn (`millturn.mch`) states only a C along Z. So no shipped mill-turn changes, and there is no end-to-end pin for the cross drill.
4. The declared capability, not a check of the post's name and not a fixture change. Three conditions:
   - **Backed by a pin.** `posting_rotaries_first.rs` posts three indexed slots through `tormach.cps`. It asserts, in each section, `G53 G0 Z` then `G0 A` before the first X/Y word. A registry check fails when a new shipped post declares the flag without an order test.
   - **A user's own script is taken at its word, never silently.** A `File` post that declares the flag puts a note on the path.
   - **The stamp follows the declaration.** The #3084 word is written only when the posed law reads the operation. So `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` (Tormach PathPilot) keeps its stamps from main, and this PR does not change it.

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse_table_tilt`:
  - `a_3_2_plane_under_the_work_a_turning_table_can_leave_turned_up_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_3_2_plane_over_every_pose_of_a_turning_table_passes`
  - `a_post_that_turns_the_table_first_reads_the_plane_at_its_own_pose`
  - `a_users_own_post_is_taken_at_its_declared_order_with_a_note` (with the negative: the same script without the flag is held by name)
- `posting_rotaries_first`:
  - `only_the_tormach_post_declares_that_it_turns_the_rotaries_first`
  - `the_tormach_post_turns_a_at_safe_z_before_each_first_xy_traverse`
- `first_traverse_table`: `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` (changed)
- lib: `the_fixed_table_reads_its_top_in_the_paths_height_scale`
- `tilt_a180_routes` and `tilt_basis0_edited_file` are unchanged. They were red on the first head, and they pass now.

## Readings (debug)

All green on head b62078f62:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`:
  - `--lib`
  - `tilt_a180_routes`, `tilt_basis0_edited_file`
  - `posting_rotaries_first`, `first_traverse_table_tilt`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_posed`
  - `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `microarc_test_part`
  - `tormach_fourth_axis`, `tormach_post`, `tormach_wrapped_a`, `tormach_machines`, `tormach_safe_retract`, `tormach_toolchange_lift`
  - `golden_cl`, `example_catalog`
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`:
  - `--lib`
  - `explain_tormach`, `script_tormach`, `tormach_no_a_word`, `tormach_rotary_travel`, `tormach_same_tool`, `probe_tormach`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Green on the merged head a4d2ac019 (main merged in): `posting_rotaries_first`, `first_traverse_table_tilt`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_posed`, `tilt_a180_routes`, `tilt_basis0_edited_file`, `first_4axis_part`.

The first head also ran the cross-drill and mill-turn suites. This head does not change them.

Heavy lanes: the diff reaches the app heavy lanes. Not run, covered by the cut gate.

## Not exercised

- The cross drill end to end. No shipped mill-turn states a tilting rotary that turns the work.
- A user's script that declares the flag and does not keep the order. It is taken at its word, with the note.
- The full quick gate. Only the binaries listed above were run.

Changelog: The first traverse of a 3+2 plane and of a cross drill, on a machine whose table tilts the work, is now judged through every pose that the previous program can leave, unless the post declares that it turns the rotaries at the safe Z before the X/Y traverse (the Tormach PathPilot post does); a clearance under the work turned up is refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation).

title: fix(contour): a None lead-in stands the wall arc entry down
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: on an outside ring, the Arc entry does not run its vertical wall arc when the lead-in is `Lead::None`. The level descends by the grazing dive at the ring's start. A note names the stand-down once.
- `crates/app/tests/contour_none_lead.rs`: new pins. Each test edits the contour through `EditOperationParams` and generates it, as the page's Apply does.
- `docs/decisions/3132-contour-none-lead.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

The report does not name the entry type. On `Milling-test.step`, only the Arc entry reproduces the symptom. Plunge, Ramp and Helix with both leads None already start the cut on the ring.

With both leads None, the Arc entry's wall arc lands on the seam itself. Its start is about 8.7 mm back along the seam's tangent. From above, that arc is a straight move into the seam. It has the same shape as the seeded 8 mm linear lead. An Arc lead changes the shape, and a Linear lead keeps it, as the report says.

## Tests

Pins, all in `contour_none_lead`:
- `arc_entry_with_both_leads_none_starts_the_cut_on_the_ring`: Linear to None, Lead out None, zero extensions, zero overlap, Arc entry. The first XY cut is flat at the level and starts on the ring's closed seam. The post has no G18/G19.
- `plunge_entry_with_both_leads_none_starts_the_cut_on_the_ring`: the same check for the Plunge entry.
- `linear_and_arc_leads_keep_their_shapes`: Linear gives an 8 mm straight lead, and Arc gives an arc lead. A change back to None removes the lead.
- `arc_entry_with_a_linear_lead_still_descends_on_its_arc`: the wall arc still runs when there is a lead.

Mutation check: with `contour.rs` from `upstream/main`, `arc_entry_with_both_leads_none_starts_the_cut_on_the_ring` fails (move 2 from (9.711, -34.723, 20.0) is not on the ring). With the fix, it passes. The other three pins pass on both versions. They are regression guards.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, with 26 steps and 0 failed. These include `wall_arc_entry`, `arc_entry`, `vertical_arc_entry`, `entry_arc`, `solid_law_goldens` and the motion lib. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The user's project `O4 Cam Plate master` is not available here. The fix follows the one reproduction on `Milling-test.step`. If the user's entry is not Arc, reopen the issue with the entry type.
- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. Not run is not a pass.
- The bore side (Side::Inside) Arc entry does not change. In a bore, the ramp, helix and arc are certified entries in bounded air. The decision file gives the reason.
- With a tool that is not centre-cutting, an Arc entry, and no lead-in, the graze's centre-cutting refusal now applies. Its hint "pick the Arc entry" does not help in that case. A wording follow-up can name the lead.

## Overlaps

PR #3120 changes `lead_fit.rs`, `lead_seam.rs` and `mod.rs`. This PR does not change those files, so there is no overlap.

Changelog: A 2D Contour with both lead shapes set to None no longer keeps a straight entry at the seam: the Arc entry's wall arc stands down and the level dives at the ring's start (#3132).

Fixes #3132

body:

Each of the 12 catalog cases now has `case.toml` with `kinds`, `machine` and `expect`.

Filtered commands still validate links across the whole catalog.

The catalog README documents the supported flat TOML format.
The decision record explains the schema and generation choices.

## Cause

They did not read case metadata or check operation-page links.

- `catalog_check_rejects_missing_case_metadata`
- `catalog_check_rejects_unknown_case_kind`
- `catalog_check_rejects_missing_case_link`

Additional pins cover generation and metadata:

title: fix(multiaxis): refuse a work-turning rotary line off the WCS origin
body:
Stacked on #3125 (merge #3125 first).

## What changed

- New function `posting::index_swing::off_origin`. It is true when a rotary states a `pivot` or an `offset` that is not zero, or not finite.
- The index-swing clause (`posting_index_swing::verdict`) has a new verdict `OffOrigin`. A work-turning rotary with a level line and an off-origin `pivot` or `offset` refuses the post by name. With two or more work-turning rotaries, any off-origin rotary refuses.
- The posed first-traverse law (`operation::first_traverse_posed::turn_of`) refuses generation by name in the same cases.
- One vertical work-turning rotary with a pivot is not refused. A turn about a vertical line keeps every height.
- A zero `pivot` or `offset` is judged as before.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3127-offset-rotary-line.md`.

## Cause

The two clauses read each work-turning rotary line through the WCS origin. A machine file can state a `pivot` or an `offset` that moves the line. The clauses then read the swept set about the wrong line. The reading can be too low, and the post is not blocked.

`pivot` is in machine coordinates. The project does not state where the WCS origin is in machine coordinates. So the program cannot place the moved line. A refusal is the safe answer.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`:
  - `a_table_line_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_by_name` (red before the fix: "no refusal: Ok []").
  - `a_zero_pivot_reads_the_table_line_through_the_wcs_origin` (clear case).
- `crates/app/tests/index_swing_offset_line.rs` (new file):
  - `a_pivot_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_the_index_swing_by_name` (red before the fix).
  - `an_offset_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_the_index_swing_by_name` (red before the fix).
  - `a_zero_pivot_and_offset_judge_the_index_swing_as_before` (clear case; the program posts).
- Mutation: with the two source files put back to the #3125 head, the three refusal pins fail and the two clear pins pass. With the fix, all five pass.
- `index_swing` (13) and `first_traverse_posed` (5) pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, local, debug): 9 steps, 0 failed. Steps: app lib, `first_traverse_posed`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `index_swing_offset_line`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `setup_mount_trace`.

## Goldens moved

None. No shipped machine file states `pivot` or `offset`.

## Not exercised

- The two-rotary branch of `turn_of` with an off-origin rotary has no own pin. It uses the same `off_origin` test as the pinned single-rotary branch.
- A vertical rotary with a pivot (not refused) has no own pin.

## Overlaps

- #3125: this PR is stacked on it. It changes `turn_of` in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse_posed.rs` and adds tests to `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`.
- #2831 touches `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs`. This PR puts its index-swing pins in a new file, so there is no overlap.

Changelog: A work-turning rotary whose machine file states a non-zero pivot or offset now refuses the index-swing check and the posed first-traverse check by name, instead of a reading about a line through the WCS origin.

Effort: high

Fixes #3127

title: fix(slot): cut the round ends of a slot wider than the tool
body:
## What changed

- A Slot wider than its tool now runs one wall lap at each level, after the rows.
- The lap follows the boundary of the tool centre stadium: two straight sides and two half circles.
- Each half circle is a chain of arcs (G02/G03). The chain is split at every row end on it and at its tip, so no arc is more than 90 degrees.
- The rows and the lap compute a row end with one function (`cap_point`). Each row join meets the lap at the same point to the bit.
- The lap starts where the last row ends and closes at that point.
- Under `climb` the lap is counterclockwise (the slot's air on the left, the same sense as the rows). Under conventional it is clockwise.
- A full-width slot (`h = 0`, one row on the centre line) does not change.
- The lap code is in the new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_lap.rs`. `slots.rs` is 394 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2906-slot-round-ends.md`.

## Cause

A row touches a round end only at its end point. The move between two rows is a straight line. The tool did not follow the arc between two row ends. On a 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool, 0.86 mm stayed on the wall of each round end.

## Why the arcs are split at the row ends

The first version used two quarter arcs for each cap. The quick gate refused it on 8 app suites. The verifier's crossing law (a) flattens an arc into chords inside its circle. A row join is a chord that ends exactly on the circle, so it crossed those flattened chords, and the post was held. With the split, the join and the lap share their vertices. The law reads a shared vertex as a touch, not a crossing. The crossing law does not change.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_climb`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_conventional`
  - `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends`
  - Each point on the stadium wall must be within the tool radius of the tool centre path (limit 0.01 mm). No tool centre point may leave the cutter centre stadium. `crossed_pairs` (the verifier's crossing law) must be empty.
  - Red before the fix: `climb=true z=9: 0.855 mm left on the wall at (28.536, 18.536)`.
- New unit tests in `slot_lap.rs`: the lap closes on its start; each row end is a lap vertex; CCW from `b` runs the +n side first; CW from `b` turns round `b` first.
- Mutations:
  - `slots.rs` set back to `upstream/main`: the pin fails (0.855 mm, both directions). Restored: green.
  - The cap split without the row ends (tangent points and tip only): `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends` fails with 22 crossing pairs. Restored: green.
- Expected-change test updates:
  - `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`: `slot_offsets_rows_across_a_wide_channel`, `conventional_slot_starts_at_the_far_end`, `slot_stock_to_leave_narrows_the_center_area` read the rows as the prefix of the level and pin the lap (arc count, direction, tips at x = -7 and 47, close at the last row end). `slot_helix_orbits_in_the_certified_channel` counts only descending arcs as the helix.
  - `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` (`an_entry_edit_marks_the_slot_stale_and_the_orbit_proves_itself`): an orbit is a descending arc. The planar arcs are the lap.
  - `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_2d_slots.rs`: the Slot now has 8 arc blocks (4 for each level).
  - `crates/app/tests/clearance_in_stock.rs` (`a_slot_traverse_at_a_clearance_plane_inside_the_stock_is_convicted_and_holds_the_post`): see "Side effect" below.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `35020f6cc`: 732 steps, 0 failed.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Side effect (please check in review)

In `clearance_in_stock`, the slot's lateral traverse between its levels was convicted only because the uncut crescents of the round ends stood in its path. The traverse stays inside the slot's own channel. With the ends cut, the verifier acquits it. The plane is still convicted by the first traverse (`FirstTraverseLow`, #2901) and by the rapid from the plane down into the stock (`RapidInStock { at: 1 }`). The post is still held with "travels through stock". The test now asserts these facts.

## Goldens moved

All in `slot_wide_channel_rows` and the catalog case `2d/slots`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/slot_wide_channel_rows.cl`: 12 lap moves added (2 lines, 10 arcs; each cap split at the rows -7, -3, 1, 5, 7 and the tip). The header changes from `v1` to `v2` because the CL now has arcs.
- The NC golden of each dialect (`nc/`, `carvera`, `doosan-dnm`, `grbl`, `grblhal`, `haas`, `heidenhain`, `linuxcnc`, `mach4`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `tinyg`, `tormach`, `tormach/explain_`): the same 12 moves added. In `heidenhain` and `sinumerik` the block numbers after the lap move up. No other line changes.
- Catalog case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` (`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots`):
  - `slots.nc`: 6 lap moves added at each of the two levels (rows at -2, 0, 2: each cap is two quarter arcs).
  - `slots.camproj`: the cached Slot moves gain the lap. The stamps change.
  - The first rapid's `from` of the two operations changes from `(0, 0)` to the start point. This change is also in the Trochoidal slot, which this PR does not change. It is drift of the catalog file on main, written by the catalog tool. I kept the tool's output and did not edit it by hand.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run. The change is in `motion` and reaches the `app` heavy lanes. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The app's `verify` was not run by hand on the catalog case. The suites that post it (`example_catalog`, `solid_law_goldens`) are green.
- Ramp and Helix entries with the lap ran only through the existing slot tests.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot*.rs` or the catalog case `2d/slots`. The branch merges cleanly with the current `main` (`8be100737`).

Changelog: A Slot wider than its tool now cuts its two round ends to size with a wall lap at each level; before, up to 0.86 mm stayed on the end walls.

Effort: high

Fixes #2906

title: fix(2d): close Zigzag pockets with wall and island rings
body:
## What changed
- A 2D pocket that cuts as Zigzag now closes with one ring on each boundary loop of the cutter-center area. Auto resolves to Zigzag, so Auto gets the rings too. The rings cut the outer wall and each island wall.
- The pocket uses the existing rest-pocket plan (`pocket_zigzag::rest_passes`). The rows stand 0.01 mm inside the area, and the rings follow the area boundary.
- The row points now stand on the 1 um lattice.
- A Zigzag pocket with blended turns now holds its blends to the crossing law (`hold_crossings`), as the rest pocket does. A fillet that would cross a ring stays a sharp turn.

## Cause
- `pocket_over_with_relief` used the rows-only plan for an ordinary Zigzag pocket. Only rest pockets got the closing rings.
- The rows touch a side wall or an island only at their ends. A cusp stays between each two ends over the full depth.
- With a 6 mm tool and a 2 mm stepover, the cusp is 0.17 mm on a straight wall and 0.75 mm on an R4 corner. Verify has no law for that material, so the program passed as clean.
- Two more problems came from the change itself:
  - The 0.01 mm gap puts the row ends off the lattice. A helix entry snaps its turns to the lattice. Two levels' helices at one off-lattice start then differed by 3.5e-7 mm, and the post check read them as crossings (`setup_align`). Lattice row points remove this.
  - Blended row turns crossed the new rings (`app corner_blend`). The crossing hold removes this.

## Tests
New pins: `crates/motion/tests/pocket_wall_finish.rs`. The pocket is 60 x 40, with R4 corners and a 16 mm island. The tool is 6 mm, with a 2 mm stepover.
- `auto_pocket_with_island_finishes_walls_and_island`
- `zigzag_pocket_with_island_finishes_walls_conventional`
- `zigzag_pocket_without_island_finishes_walls`
- `blended_zigzag_pocket_finishes_walls_without_crossings`
- `blended_zigzag_turns_do_not_cross_the_closing_rings`

The first four tests measure the scallop on each wall at the floor. The limit is 0.02 mm. They also check `verify::crossed_pairs`.

Red before the fix: the first four tests fail on unchanged code (outer wall scallop 0.755 mm; 0.919 mm when blended).

Mutation checks:
1. Old `pocket.rs` guard: the 4 wall pins go red. Restored: green.
2. No lattice snap in `rest_passes`: `setup_align::the_pocket_and_face_kinds_cut_the_flipped_part_and_post` goes red ("post blocked - 4 warning(s): ... cross in XY at shared depth"). Restored: green.
3. No crossing hold for Zigzag: `blended_zigzag_turns_do_not_cross_the_closing_rings` goes red (12 crossing pairs, the same pairs as `app corner_blend`). Restored: green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 6e3e4397b: 678 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Expected-change test: `setup_align` asserted the island clearance with a square box (`max(|x|, |y|) < 21.9`). A closing ring at a rounded corner is legal but failed that check. The assertion now measures the Euclidean distance to the 40 x 40 block (at least 1.9 mm for the 4 mm tool).

## Goldens moved
There are 18 changed files, all for one pocket case and the two first-part sample programs:
- `crates/app/tests/golden/pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island.cl` and `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island_blended.cl`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/*/pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island.nc`: 12 dialects, plus the Tormach `explain_` file.
- `examples/first-part.nc` and `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc`. The 2D Pocket1 of that part is Auto.

In each NC file, only motion blocks change: the rows move 0.01 mm inward, and the ring blocks are new. Block numbers after them move by the same count. No header, tool, spindle or coolant line changes. The `.camproj` files do not change.

## Not exercised
- The QA project from the report (`q01-first-post.camproj` on skull). The motion pin rebuilds the same shape.
- `pocket_avoid` (Do not touch) and the 3D pocket levels still cut Zigzag rows with no ring. #3129 tracks them.
- A pre-existing defect: in a narrow band, two helix entries of different passes can overlap. The post check blocks it. That is before and after this change. #3129 notes it.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run.

## Overlaps
- #2842 touches `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_emit.rs` (the level ladder line). This PR does not change that file.

Changelog: 2D Pocket with strategy Zigzag or Auto now finishes the pocket walls and islands with a closing pass, so no wall scallops stay above the stock to leave.

title: fix(kernel): measure a fan at a spline pole by its true sag
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/kernel/src/mesh_pole.rs`. It finds a triangle corner that sits on a pole of a spline face. At a pole, the derivative along one parameter is zero.
- The module moves the free parameter of that corner to the mean of the other two corners. It takes those two corners on one side of the period.
- The module keeps the move only when the surface point stays within 1e-9 mm.
- `mesh_deviation::face` calls the module for spline faces before it samples a triangle. Analytic faces do not change.
- New fixture `testdata/models/sphere_quarter_pole.step`. This is our own file: a quarter sphere, R 25, with a rational B-spline dome that turns 180 degrees and ends in a pole at the apex.

## Cause

The issue reports an open mesh on v0.24.0. On upstream/main 8be100737 (after #917), the import itself refuses the q02 part:

```
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 10 is the ellipsoid boss (`#3666`, a rational B-spline with a pole at its top). The mesh is good. Its sag against the ellipsoid is about 0.004 mm. The planner gives the apex node u = 0 (and u = 1), and the ring under it has u near 0.5. The measure interpolated u across half the period in each fan triangle. It then projected from a hint on the far side of the surface. The bound of those triangles became 0.29 mm. The bound did not change at a finer chord. This showed that the measure was wrong and the mesh was not.

## Readings (q02 STEP from the QA host, local only)

- Before: the import refuses with the message above.
- After: 48780 facets, 0 open edges.
- After: the volume is 97163.50 mm^3. SolidCraft gives 97165.69 mm^3.
- After: the slice at z = 19.6875 (the reported height) gives 1382.27 mm^2. Slices at z = 18.5, 20, 25 and 29 also close.

## Tests

Pins:
- `camcraft-kernel` `mesh_deviation_pole::a_fan_at_a_spline_pole_measures_by_its_true_sag`. Red before the fix: "a good fan at a pole is judged 0.1065280187198439 mm off".
- `camcraft-kernel` `mesh_deviation_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_meshes_inside_the_tolerance`. Red before the fix: "face Some(2) stands 2.775e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm" (the same refusal as q02).
- `camcraft-app` `import_step_spline_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_imports_closed_and_slices`. Red before the fix with the same refusal. Green after: volume and five slices.
- `camcraft-kernel` lib `mesh_pole::tests` (3 unit tests).

Mutation: I put back `mesh_deviation.rs` from upstream/main. The three pins above went red. I restored the fix. The pins went green.

Original author gate results:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 90 steps. 89 were green on the first run. The one red step was `kernel suites: step_agreement` (`step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`: "a fixture has no row"). That test requires a row for each STEP fixture. I added the row for `sphere_quarter_pole.step` (`Truck::NotRecorded`, the form for fixtures after #2790) and its `per_file!` test. The bench reads the file as "watertight, within tolerance", V = 16358.3 mm^3 (exact pi R^3 / 3 = 16362.5). After that, `step_agreement` is green: 27 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Review follow-up

Head: `bb6480b6554f66a31c0158fbf1a80a9adc81cfa3` (unchanged).
Base: `upstream/main` at `60cb97a0b3717bf6a129e781fd8f4ec98806124b`.

title: fix(2d): read a drafted side as a wall, not as a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

- A no-pick 2D chamfer now reads a drafted side as a wall. It does not read it as a modelled chamfer.
- The chamfer takes a third section of the material, half way between the top plane and the corner plane.
- A piece of a top loop is a drafted wall when two conditions are true:
  - It stands off the wall by no more than `depth * tan(15 deg)`.
  - The half-depth section stands half that distance off the wall within `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm). This check limits the departure from a straight wall.
- A loop with drafted pieces and no bevelled piece rides its wall at the corner depth. It counts with the sharp loops (#2596). Thus a plate with no modelled chamfer breaks every edge, the drafted side and the pocket included.
- `partly_bevelled` becomes `read`, which returns a `Reading`. The #2887 refusal text does not change.
- `ride_loops` takes two new arguments: `mid` (the half-depth section) and `depth`. The one caller, `material_source.rs`, makes the half-depth section.

## Cause

PR #2894 refuses a loop that is bevelled on only part of its length. It reads each piece more than 0.05 mm off the wall as "bevelled". A drafted side also stands off the wall. With a 1 mm chamfer and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is more than 0.05 mm off. The plate was refused with a "modelled chamfer" message.

Two sections cannot tell a draft from a small modelled chamfer. A third section checks the straight slope within the section grid slack. A draft puts the half-depth section at half the offset. A modelled chamfer that ends before the corner plane departs from this slope. The review found that a 25% residual allowance admitted a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The check now uses `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm).

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride_tests.rs`:

- `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall`: #2887's plate with its X0 side drafted 3.5, 5 and 10 degrees. Red on unchanged code: `the edge loop near X0.087 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length`.
- `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft`: a 0.2 mm modelled bevel on one side is still refused.
- `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: the review fixture has a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The test requires the partial-bevel refusal for a 1 mm ride.
- `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer`: a 45 degree bevel deeper than the ride is still refused.
- The #2887 tests (`a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `..._with_an_extra_vertex_too`) still pass. The old test calls go through a small `ride` helper.

Mutation checks (each guard taken out, then put back):

- Drafted reading off: `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall` red.
- Half-depth check off: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` red.
- Slope limit off: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` red.
- Drafted match arm after the vertex-gap arm: the 3.5 degree case of the drafted pin red (it rode the top loop, inside the part).

Review verification on head `5e745b74430e4186f3bf293a23aa8b462a217fba`:

- Mutation check for `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: RED with the former `d * 0.25` allowance (0 passed, 1 failed; exit 101). Restoring `LEAN_SLACK` gives GREEN: all 17 `chamfer_ride` library tests pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. The run completed 139 steps in 84 minutes: 138 passed and 1 failed. Test totals: 1938 passed, 1 failed, 64 ignored.
- The sole quick failure is `adaptive_troch_parallel::wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes`. It took 130.0258 seconds, above its 90-second wall-clock limit. The narrow `--failed` retry with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=1` also failed at 98.172 seconds. This review fix does not change that test or its limit.
- Motion library: 494 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored. App library: 292 passed, 0 failed. `chamfer_modelled_edge`: 7 passed. `chamfer_partly_bevelled`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, 2 minutes 39 seconds.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 235 steps passed in 80.5 minutes. The reached plan ran all motion and app heavy targets, with no manual skips. The 35 motion steps passed 57 tests. The 193 app steps passed 43 tests. Total: 100 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Six standard expected-failure validations (#1950: 3; #2849: 3) failed as expected. The plan also had one build step.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

title: fix(2d): turn a contour seam lead only when it crosses its own ring
body:
## What changed
- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_seam.rs` with `seam_tangents`.
- `lead_fit.rs` calls `seam_tangents` from `both_fit` and `plan_leads`.
- At the seam of a closed ring, the function builds the full lead along the walk's end tangent.
- It checks that lead against the ring's own feed moves. It uses the verifier's crossing law (`arc_cross::moves_cross_prior`).
- Only a lead that crosses gets a new tangent: the old tangent mirrored across the other end's tangent.
- The mirrored lead is used only if it does not cross.
- A lead that does not cross keeps its tangent. Open walks keep their tangents.
- New test file `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/3019-contour-lead-cross-only.md`.

## Cause
- On the issue's R6 plate, the seam falls on a fitted corner arc.
- The 8 mm linear lead-out along that arc's end tangent crossed the ring's long bottom edge next to the seam. The lead-in did the same on a conventional cut.
- Verify found one crossing on each level. Tabs are not the cause: the same crossing occurs with no tabs.
- The first fix (#3053) mirrored the tangent on each closed ring that bent at the seam. That also changed plain rectangles with no crossing (#3111). #3114 reverted it.
- This fix changes a lead only when that lead crosses its own ring.

## Tests
Pins (120 x 80 plate, four R6 corners, D10 tool, stepdown 3, 12 deep, linear lead 8):
- `an_outside_tabbed_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing` (climb, 4 tabs).
- `an_outside_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing_with_or_without_tabs` (climb with 0 tabs; conventional with 0 and 4 tabs).
- Each case asserts no `crossed_pairs`, no `Crossing` or `Gouge` from `verify`, and a full 8 mm lead-in and lead-out.
- The regression pin of #3111 is `vertical_arc_entry` (motion and post). It is green on this head.

- M3, lead-in mirror removed: the conventional case red (`[[3, 12], [19, 28], [35, 44], [51, 60]]`).
- M4, crossing check replaced by the #3053 bend law: motion `vertical_arc_entry` red (`an_oblique_first_cut_stays_chords_and_says_so_once`, `an_x_aligned_first_cut_enters_on_one_g18_arc_per_level`). This shows that the crossing check keeps other rings unchanged.

Gate (macOS arm64, final head `8b17c42d7f804d8409bc1ad2ddf3e3699b675815`):

Base: upstream/main `f036dddad0de170aad9cd07a56ec3d53589ac517`.

title: fix(circular): keep the helix entries of the rings apart
body:
## What changed

- A flat Circular with a helix entry turns the start of each later ring. The new start is a vertex of the ring's own polygon. At that vertex, the predicted helix orbit keeps 0.01 mm from the orbits that the earlier rings flew.
- After each ring, the kernel reads the descents that the ring flew. It uses the crossing law itself (`verify::crossed_pairs`, 0.01 mm and 0.001 mm chords). If a descent crosses a descent of an earlier ring, the operation is refused by name: `helix entry: the descent at ... crosses the descent of an earlier ring ...`.
- The first ring and each ring without a conflict keep vertex 0. Plunge entry, ramp entry and the vault mode do not change.
- The new logic is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular_helix.rs`.
- The test module of `circular.rs` moved to `circular_tests.rs` (the `#[path]` pattern). `circular.rs` was 411 lines. It is now 374 lines.

## Cause

All rings of a flat Circular run the same level ladder. Thus the helix of each ring shares each level's depth band with the helix of each other ring. The descent puts each helix next to the ring start, and all rings started at the +X vertex. With stepover 2 and helix radius 1, the helices touched. The crossing law reported each pair, and verification blocked the post.

## Tests

title: fix(3d): an Adaptive fallback to Offset rings raises a warning
body:
Stacked on #3062 (merge #3062 first).

This PR is partial work on #3035. It does the warning part only.

## What changed

- `camcraft_sim::verify::Warning` has a new variant, `StrategyFallback { at, areas }`.
  - It is advisory. `blocks_post` is false.
  - `at` is the first cutting move. `areas` is the number of areas that the Offset rings cut in place of the Adaptive plan.
- Generate (`operation/generate.rs`) counts the fallback notes and adds the warning when the count is more than zero.
  - The op now reports `warnings` > 0 in MCP `get_job` and `generate`.
  - MCP `verify` lists the finding as `strategy_fallback` with `blocks_post: false`.
  - The UI folds the warning on its own key (225).
- `machining2d::RINGS_FALLBACK` holds the note tail `" - Offset rings cut "`. The 2D door (`pocket_hsm`) and the 3D ladder (`machining3d::hsm::rings_tag`) both use it. `machining2d::rings_fallbacks` counts the notes by it. The note text does not change.
- The rest pass and the offset shells are not counted. Their Offset rings are by design, not a fallback.

## Cause

The planner wrote each fallback to Offset rings only into the path notes. The op status stayed `ok` with `warnings=0`. In the QA run, 14 levels fell back and nothing showed it except the notes.

title: fix(app): a 3+2 first-traverse refusal names the heights the user set
body:
## What changed

- `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`) gets the field `tilted: bool` with `#[serde(default)]`. A cache saved before this change still loads, and reads as upright.
- `operation::first_traverse::judge` (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`) puts a 3+2 verdict into the frame in which the user sets the heights. Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame. The new `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` back to the two heights and sets `tilted` when the frame is not upright. The sim law does not change.
- A tilted verdict has a new text. It names the heights that the user set, says that they are measured along the tilted tool axis, and gives the raise. It has no `Z` value and no `X/Y`. The text of an upright verdict does not change.
- Guide: a troubleshooting entry for the new text (`site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md`), and one paragraph in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md` that says what the warning gives after a regenerate.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2991-tilted-first-traverse-message.md`.

## Readings

`examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`, `Indexed Face1` (B 20 deg, tilt origin Z 20, Fixed clearance height 30). The operation cache was removed in a scratch copy, so `camcraft-cli process` generated it again:

- Before: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z10.000, under the stock top at Z11.114 - raise the clearance height above Z11.114`
- After: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown position at the clearance height 30.000 mm, under the stock top at 31.114 mm (both measured along the tilted tool axis) - raise the clearance height by at least 1.114 mm`

A clearance height of 31.114 or more passes the law (the local value is then 11.114 or more).

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse::a_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis` (app): the verdict gives the typed clearance (25, not the local 5), the corner in the same frame (25.209), `tilted: true`, the new text without `Z` or `X/Y`, and the post refusal with the raise. It fails without the change in `judge` (`tilted` stays false).
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_tilted_verdict_names_the_raise_not_a_z_value` (sim): the full tilted text and a serde round trip.
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_verdict_saved_before_tilted_reads_as_upright` (sim): a cache JSON without `tilted` loads as upright, with the old text.
- `docs_troubleshooting` (app): the new troubleshooting heading matches the source text.

## Gates

Head 8c8a002f3 (main aa4c785db merged in, plus the test commit for main's two new 3+2 tests):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the merge c56bd62d6: 117 steps, 115 ok. The 2 red steps were `first_traverse_table` and `first_traverse_mill_turn` (main's tests that pin the local frame). After 8c8a002f3, `--failed` re-ran them: 2 of 2 ok.
- Touched app binaries on 8c8a002f3: `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `clearance_in_stock`, `stale_rapid_law`, `wcs_start`: 35 passed, 0 failed. The `sim` and `app` lib tests for `first_traverse`: 17 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on 8c8a002f3: 236 steps (198 app, 37 motion), 0 failed, wall time 62.5 min. The 12 known-fail steps (#1950 and others) are red as expected.

Earlier, on head 9eee9c59d (before the merge of main): quick 109 steps and heavy 234 steps, 0 failed; `docs_troubleshooting` pass; clippy for `sim`, `app` and `ui` clean.

## Not exercised

- A saved cache keeps its old text until the operation is generated again. The verdict and the held post do not change. I did not change the op stamp salt, because that moves each stamp (`deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`, the example projects) for a text change. For the same reason I did not regenerate `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`. The decision file records the two choices.
- No GUI check of the Warnings pane. The pane shows the `Display` text that the tests pin.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 44), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

- Review fix on `aded58c47` (merged with `upstream/main` `f036dddad`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 694 steps, 1 failed. The red step is `app suites: tool_gate` (`the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry`). Its red row is `OpType::Finish3D`: `upstream/main` (#3069) adds `Router ball nose 6 mm` before `BN-0600` in the catalog, and the tie goes to the first entry. The step is red on `upstream/main` too. The waterjet row in the same test passes.
  - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 237 steps, 0 failed. The lanes are `motion heavy` (37 steps), `app heavy` (199 steps) and the heavy build.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.
- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe. This is follow-up #3047.
- The MCP skill row. The skill file is a protected path in this session. This is follow-up #3048.
- The UI page was not opened in an interactive window. The screenshots below come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell.

## Screenshots

The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch (commit `4dad162f3`, folder `pr-3058/v2/`). They come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell on the same machine. The render code is not committed.

title: feat(ui): place DXF profiles on the stock from the Stock page and a drop
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:
  - "Profile X", "Profile Y" and "Profile angle (deg)". These are a draft. "Place profile" queues one `MoveSketch`.
  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `camcraft_geometry::dxf`, so the UI can name the `Primitive` variants. This adds no crate dependency.

The import does not use `finish_import`. That function handles the model worker. `ImportDxf` checks the drawing at construction, so the typed `DxfUnitsMissing` error is caught where the UI builds the command. `docs/decisions/1863-dxf-stock-ui.md` records this and the other choices.

## Cause

The #1862 commands had no UI door. A user could place a DXF profile only through MCP or the script.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/dxf_profile.rs`:

- `the_stock_page_adds_lists_places_and_deletes_a_dxf_profile`
- `a_drawing_without_units_asks_millimeters_or_inches_and_never_guesses`
- `a_dropped_dxf_lands_on_the_stock_or_asks_for_one`
- `the_browser_lists_the_profile_under_its_stock_with_an_eye`
- `the_viewport_draws_the_chains_on_the_stock_top_and_marks_open_ends`
- `the_operation_page_takes_the_profile_as_its_source_without_a_model`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_profile_lines_and_a_move_builds_once`

Also:

title: feat(mcp): compact read modes and chat context budgets
body:
## What changed

MCP read modes for small context windows (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`. Each operation keeps only the `params` fields that differ from the kind defaults. Null and empty fields outside `params` are removed.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (key or label) and `section`. An unknown name is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the name and the pick facts. Counts replace the loops. The compact default `limit` is 25. The full default stays 500.
- `provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet::Core)` gives a core set of 25 workflow tools. `tools(provider)` is unchanged.
- The new code is in `mcp/compact.rs`. `job.rs`, `features.rs`, `pick.rs` and `tools.rs` get small hooks only.

Chat worker limits (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):

- A tool reply to the model is cut at 12000 JSON characters, with a hint that names the compact modes. The tool card keeps the full text.
- A request carries at most one viewport image (the newest).
- A turn stops after 12 model rounds. The old `MAX_TURN_STEPS` moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and now has a test.
- A request carries at most 6 earlier turns. When older turns are dropped, the latest `get_job` reply goes in front of the first kept prompt.
- A local endpoint gets the core tool set. A cloud endpoint gets the full table.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1944-ai-context-budgets.md`.

## Cause

Enhancement. The full tool table and one full `get_job` or `list_features` reply can fill the context window of a small local model.

## Tests

The results in this section apply to original head `398a4a937a6267dce87da97495149713412920a5`.
The final-head results are in "Latest review findings" below.

Pins (all new; network is not used):

- `crates/app/tests/mcp_compact.rs`: `get_job_summary_drops_the_machine_definition_and_default_fields`, `get_job_summary_refuses_a_non_boolean`, `list_operation_types_filters_by_kind_and_by_section`, `list_features_compact_rows_are_short_and_the_default_limit_is_chat_sized`, `the_core_tool_set_is_a_small_subset_of_the_full_table`. Each asserts a character budget.
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::budget`: `a_long_tool_reply_is_cut_to_the_character_cap_with_a_hint`, `a_local_model_gets_the_core_tool_set_and_a_cloud_model_the_full_table`, `a_turn_stops_at_the_round_cap`.
- `egui_app::ai_chat::budget::tests`: `a_cut_keeps_whole_characters_and_says_how_much_was_shown`, `a_small_reply_passes_and_a_long_one_is_one_capped_text_block`, `only_the_newest_image_goes_with_a_request`, `old_turns_are_dropped_and_the_latest_get_job_reply_is_kept`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pin red; code restored, pin green):

- `turn.rs` from upstream: the image pin and the history pin are red.

Original-head gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed (131 steps, 0 failed). Original-head clippy passed. That head later conflicted with upstream main. The final-head results below replace these results.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code changes.

## Not exercised

- A real provider endpoint. The tests use the scripted transport.

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions or lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.

- #2920 and #2716: `features.rs` views and `list_features`; `tools.rs` `list_features` row (this PR adds three lines in `list_features` and edits the `get_job` and `list_operation_types` rows).

Changelog: AI chat keeps large jobs inside the model's context: compact MCP read modes (`get_job` summary, `list_operation_types` kind/section filter, `list_features` compact), a core tool set for local models, and caps on tool reply size, images, rounds and history.

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...814dca499f9f9793f3c9e6bcd3eafab5f32e2022).

## Author gate status

The guarded source at cfc281268 passed the complete reached heavy gate, 247/247 steps in 58.1 minutes on macOS arm64. It includes the separate default-machine correction merged upstream in #3092. The mixed-condition regression passed in the 19-test Agie writer module. Both input orders received the exact error and no files.

On the corrected production source 766fc7109, the regular CLI exported all 20 synthetic jobs. Their 32 works and 72 native files matched the previous guarded outputs byte for byte. All 20 controller-review receipts matched. All 20 repeat attempts refused to replace an existing job and preserved every byte. This corpus is a software comparison. The real control checks below cover the stated representative jobs.

The full quick gate on 766fc7109 found the missing dedicated test suite for the built-in Agie CPS dispatcher. The next commit added the suite and its 11 expected refusal records. Passing each record requires the direct single-file post to fail with the native-job diagnostic and leave no NC file.

The final head is 814dca499. It changes only tests above cfc281268. On a real plasma stream and 1300PL machine, the Agie single-file dispatcher must fail with its specific native-directory diagnostic. The workspace must exclude the post from the plasma registry. The single-file smoothing test now uses the workspace's native-post predicate. With smoothing enabled, a mounted Agie punch must refuse the setup and create no job directory. The other posts retain their previous checks.

All 49 targeted tests passed on the final head: seven plasma, seven smoothing, 12 native app, 11 native dispatcher and 12 recorded-stream tests.

The original full quick on cfc281268 ran 1,013 steps in 80.6 minutes. All but the two cross-post tests passed, including strict Clippy. On 814dca499 the official failed-step replay selected both suites and passed both in 0.8 minutes. Each suite ran seven tests. The complete 247-step heavy result belongs to cfc281268. The whole quick and heavy gates have not been repeated on 814dca499.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6 --failed gate-logs/quick-20261121-023002
```

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Integration order

The maintainer requests a separate P1 change from main and a safety-tier review of each feature PR. The standalone zero-step encoder is #3104. The first workspace writer in #2951 uses it. Keep earlier feature drafts that still generate erosion steps on hold until each takes its own safety correction and review. The standalone machine template in #2948 has no writer.

## Gate commands and pinning tests

The earlier macOS bore fixture and missing operation name were reproduced on ba5ff0ae1 with these commands:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c --only 'app suites: default_machine_missing'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c --only 'app heavy: pocket3d_hsm'
```

The scoped CLI and native writer checks include:

- `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour`
- `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality`
- `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`
- `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero`
- `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. Later changes clarify the repeat-import result and pin the refusal for mixed wire conditions.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. Both screenshots show the same synthetic cutoff job, DEMO2999, after the desktop Post command. The new receipt lists the control checks and the offsets of 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.

**Before · `feb802a77`**

![Earlier Post receipt reporting three files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-before.png)

**After · `814dca499`**

![Current Post receipt reporting zero working steps and the required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-after.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984
