title: feat(wire): post placed DXF racetracks and circles with native Agie arcs
body:
Stacked on #2974. Review the [placed DXF wire changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/760e62cc194f49d6efb51cfd557574d7df4cede0...80daeae0852e3f46a6ebfa5b47c13aeb2689b592).

**Safety review pending on `80daeae08`.** This branch predates the zero-step writer in #2951. The control results below describe the placed DXF profile on the tested installation. Before merge or machine use, this branch must adopt the #2984 correction and verify that the control imports the work with zero erosion steps.

Use one closed DXF racetrack or circle as the source for a vertical punch. Keep the original lines and arcs through placement, normal Wire Contour generation, verification and native output. Invalidate the toolpath when the source or placement changes. The conservative preview encloses the exact arcs with at most 0.000025 mm of radial excess.

A racetrack needs two parallel cardinal straight sides tangent to two semicircles. A circle needs a radius from 6 through 15 mm and a radial threading lead on a cardinal side. The native grid must represent the circle and the intended seam. Individual chain selection, other drawings and laser work remain part of #2022.

Run the original examples from the repository root:

```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/racetrack.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/circle-punch.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/north-circle.camscript
```

The translated and 90 degree rotated R10 racetrack generated 1,409 moves with zero warnings. Agie Control kept the arc centers at (−6, 1) and (10, 1). It reported pass radii of 10.245, 10.155, 10.140 and 10.134 mm. The arc direction reversed on alternate passes. The separation on the straight section measured 1.000 mm.

On circular jobs, each bridge swept 1/R radians for a 1.000 mm nominal arc. The rough and trim wire paths stayed concentric. Three CAMCraft jobs exercised R6 east, R10 west and R15 north. Separate synthetic reference jobs checked all four cardinal directions at R10. The formal checks reported zero job errors. body:
Stacked on #2951. The parent is a fork branch. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/83affaca1bf4920ed07e29bf7c52bf9c48561b80...6b790f4dd6aa0f4e37feeb03bd16b911fb19d664).

A trial merge with the corrected parent `f92e67857` found conflicts in `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs`, and `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`. The update must preserve the entry and clearance checks for oblique faces.

Use the actual faces of a convex prismatic punch in the native Agie job. Include the control's rough-pass corner reach and the wire radius when checking the stock. Compute the separation clearance along the entry face. Keep compensation at the control and preserve the source vertices. A reentrant profile still refuses.

The original sample uses five straight sides and an oblique 3:4 entry face. The hole is at X-20.5 Y6 and the perpendicular seam is at X-12.5 Y0. The material, wire, stock thickness and QN2 settings are the same as in #2951.

Run the example using a new POLY20 destination:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript
```

On 4c715164b the quick gate passed all 84 post tests. Seven application suites passed another 52 tests. Strict all-targets Clippy passed for camcraft-post. The heavy plan selected 199 app steps. Those steps have not run for this draft.

The CLI preserved the original rectangular output byte for byte. On the oblique job it preserved all nominal vertices and the hole position. A tight acute corner and a separation or lead shorter than 3 mm produced a refusal and no output directory. Head 6b790f4dd handles a perpendicular foot between five-decimal grid points. The post keeps the hole fixed and selects an exterior point within 0.00001 mm of the true foot. It checks both split lengths and the approach using the emitted coordinates. It refuses a near-limit face if a valid grid point cannot preserve the required clearances. On the final head all 86 native post library tests and strict all-targets Clippy passed. The control plotted SLOPE20, a 7:10 face, with the four expected exterior offsets and a 1 mm final section.

Pinning tests: oblique_punch_preserves_nominal_vertices_and_perpendicular_seam and an_acute_miter_needs_more_stock_than_a_round_corner. The offline control imported the unchanged CamCraft POLY20 files. FORMALCHECK reported zero errors and listed setup, reference and option 131072 warnings. GRAFICHECK plotted all five exterior faces. Their straight-face offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm for the rough and three trims. The rough-pass 1 mm separation section followed the oblique face from X-12.696 Y0.147 to X-12.096 Y0.947. The control returned to the original hole at X-20.5 Y6. Stock was Z-20 to Z0. No physical machine cut was made.

title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**This first writer now uses the zero-step encoder from #3104. The machine template and standalone encoder have merged. The contributor has addressed the desktop review comments. A maintainer re-check is pending.** Later feature drafts still need their own safety review before they can introduce machining behavior. A stale controller quality can change the effective finish, pass count and offsets.

This change builds on the machine template in #2948 and the standalone encoder in #3104. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

On the corrected writer, the normal CLI produced the same three CCSEP20 files as the independently verified import in #3104. Only the output stem was changed from the PUNCH40 example. The copy of the actual control showed the closed punch at zero steps. FORMALCHECK blocked it until the operator assigns technology. See [the file hashes and native work details](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3104#issuecomment-7055077111). The native bytes were tested once in that replay. No physical cut was made.

On successive imports, select the newly created piece. Match its ISO, start hole and zero steps to the intended setup. Verify the effective wire, height, quality and offsets before assigning TECCUT. Run the control's graphic and formal checks on the resulting steps.

On the earlier writer, the control plotted a rough pass and three trims after automatic generation. The measured offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. That historical result does not qualify an automatic release on this or another installation.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Review changes on `f92e67857`

Commit `25e783b50` merged upstream main at `6fafa4e1f` into the contributor branch. GitHub reports the corrected head as mergeable. A local trial merge with upstream `60cb97a0b` also completed without conflicts.

On `45d6166e1`, 67 focused tests passed. Three desktop tests use the Post button and the synthetic punch. The success case checks the requested finish, all three output files and the zero-step control review. Each refusal case checks that the output directory stays empty.

- `native_post_dialog_writes_three_files_and_reports_the_required_work_checks`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_an_invalid_job_name_without_writing_files`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_per_operation_output_without_writing_files`

On that revision the quick gate passed 1,032 of 1,033 steps, including clippy. All 253 reached heavy steps passed. The only failed step was `post suites: comment_escape`. Its registry test expected a single text file from every post.

The final commit changes only `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. The test checks header escaping for all 19 text posts and checks the native directory refusal for Agie. On `f92e67857`, all 27 focused tests passed. The official quick replay selected the one failed step and passed it. The screenshot source, UI tests and production code are identical on these two revisions.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 6fafa4e1f
# On f92e67857, use the quick log directory from the first command.
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f --failed <original-quick-log-directory>
```

## Checks on reviewed revision `025ed4760` and its predecessors

At a08c802b6, all five writer tests, four standalone encoder tests and ten application integration tests passed. The normal PUNCH40 script reproduced the previous guarded ISO, SBR and SBL. A repeat export refused to replace them. Both PUNCH40 and the CCSEP20 variant returned `working_steps_generated=false` and the controller review.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib agie::tests::
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native
```

Pinning tests include `script_post_reports_the_required_control_review_and_zero_working_steps`, `stock_origin_and_fractional_setup_coordinates_are_refused_before_publication`, `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch` and `qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition`.

The earlier guarded head was 5bdbb5fe4. It includes the upstream diagnostic fix from #3092 and a dedicated recorded-stream suite for the Agie dispatcher. The single-file post entry point must refuse the Agie dispatcher. Each of 11 input streams checks the diagnostic, the failure exit code and the absence of NC output. The suite inventory also requires this post to have its own tests.

On 5bdbb5fe4 the recorded suite passed 12/12 tests. The dispatcher suite passed 11/11. All nine default-machine regression tests and all 19 native tests passed. The normal CLI and an independent Rust caller reproduced the checked setup files and the matching ISO. Both duplicate exports preserved all files. Against upstream 211105042, the full plan selects 1,017 quick steps and 251 reached heavy steps. These two full gates did not run on that head.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test default_machine_missing
```

The final head 025ed4760 adds cross-post tests. The plasma suite now runs the direct Agie dispatcher and requires its native-directory refusal. The single-file smoothing test uses the same native-post predicate as the workspace. A mounted, otherwise valid Agie punch with smoothing enabled must report the setup-option error and create no directory. The existing native test checks all three default-option files against their expected bytes.

All 48 targeted checks passed on 025ed4760: seven plasma tests, seven smoothing tests, 11 native app tests, 11 dispatcher tests and 12 common recorded-stream tests. The full quick gate passed all 1,017 steps on this revision. The reached heavy gate passed all 251 steps. Both commands exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 8be1007379be77021079a648f16fc938fd56160c
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 8be1007379be77021079a648f16fc938fd56160c
```

The selector used merge base `211105042`. A separate trial merge of this head with upstream main at `36348cda6` completed without conflicts. GitHub still reported a conflict against the older base `211105042` at the time of that check.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Desktop Post dialog and receipt

The two current images show the synthetic DEMO20 punch on review revision `45d6166e1`. The picker identifies the requested finish. After posting, the receipt reports zero working steps and lists the checks and technology assignment required on the control.

| Before · Generic ISO | After · Native Agie |
| --- | --- |
| ![Earlier Generic ISO Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/before.png) | ![Current native Agie picker with requested finish](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/after.png) |

![Successful native Agie receipt with zero working steps and required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/receipt.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: The Wire EDM desktop and script workflows can post a supported Classic Cut 2S punch as a native zero-step Agie setup directory for control review.

Fixes #2945

title: feat(2d)!: Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains
body: Stacked on #2716 (merge #2716 first) This branch starts at the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The diff against `main` shows the changes of #2716 too, until #2716 merges. The changes of this PR are the one commit `feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains`. ## What changed - A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` now take one picked chain of a DXF profile (`FeatureSel::SketchChain` or a `SketchLayer` that holds one chain). - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`. - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The typed `width` stays. - The pick seeds in its own command (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick and the seed. This is the law of #1504. - Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain. A slot that left its outline is refused by name. A slot whose ends are not the ends of its centerline is refused by name. - The verification and the stock simulation use the setup stock (`part_solid = false`), as #2716 does for the 2D Contour. - Slot parameters keep their two-point form. This branch writes project v74 for sketch selections and per-chain overrides. A v73 file steps up and keeps its protection. Older readers refuse v74 files. These picks are refused by name: - a closed chain that is not a slot outline (a rectangle, a circle): "is not a slot outline"; - an open chain that is not straight: "the picked centerline is not straight"; - more than one chain: "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain, and this selection has 2 chains"; - the whole profile as the source: "needs one picked chain"; - a channel narrower than the tool. The `Slot` refusal now gives the slot width and the tool diameter. Files: - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_line.rs` (new): `SlotBound::from_centerline`, `SlotBound::centerline` and the ends law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`: the `Room::Line` kind in each match of the room law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs`: the numbers in the "slot is narrower than the tool" refusal. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_sketch.rs` (new): resolves the picked chain to a slot room, and holds the outline test. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`: `slot_bound_of` reads sketch picks; `slot_from_picks` and `confine_slot` include the `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks; `slot_fit_of` describes a centerline. - `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`: the job reads the slot room for a `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks, and its region is the authored stadium. - `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the `Trochoidal Slot` arm judges the slot against the slot room. - `crates/app/src/operation/material_region.rs`: the preview does not read sketch slot picks as a region. - `crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch_pick.rs`: `visit_src_chains` and `transform_chain_pts` are `pub(super)`. - `crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`: the profile law admits picked chains for the two slot kinds. - `docs/decisions/1868-slot-dxf-sketches.md`: the decision. ## Cause `sketch_model::source_problem` refused picked chains of a profile for each kind but the 2D Contour. `slot_bound_of` refused sketch picks. The slot room had no centerline kind. ## Tests Pins, in `crates/app/tests/slot_dxf_sketch.rs`: - `a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` - `a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline` - `an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width` - `picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name` Pins, in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_pins.rs`: - `a_centerline_room_holds_its_two_ends_and_refuses_other_ends` - `a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name` The four app pins were red on the unchanged code. Each failed with "picked chains of a profile are not supported yet". Readings from the outline pin (4 mm tool, 10 mm outline, centres (45, 25) and (75, 25)): - seeded ends (45.000, 25.000) and (75.000, 25.000), width 10.000 mm; - cutter centre X 42.000 to 78.000 and Y 22.000 to 28.000; - stock simulation: 0 gouge cells. Mutation results. Each mutation removes one guard. Each made a pin red. The restored code is green. | Mutation | Result | |---|---| | M1 outline area test off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M2 one-chain rule off | red (same pin) | | M3 centerline straightness test off | red (same pin) | | M4 centerline ends law off | red (`an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width`) | | M5 slot room judge off in the `Trochoidal Slot` arm | red (`a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline`) | | M6 whole-profile refusal off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M7 old profile law back | red (all four app pins) | | M8 old "narrower than the tool" text back | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M9 doubled-back centerline test off | red (`a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name`) | | M10 sketch read off in `slot_bound_of` | red (all four app pins) | Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2716` on head `bd24b9328`, where `base-2716` is the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The gate ran in two parts (`--only motion --only "app build"`, then `--only "app suites" --only "ui build" --only "ui suites"`). Result: 645 steps, 644 green, 1 red. - The red step is `app suites: feature_edge_g1_join`, test `no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture` ("bar_cross_holes.step: 116 pairs"). This is the known failure of #2713. Its fix (#2731, merge `b02b344d6`) is on `main` and is not in the branch of #2716. This PR changes no import code and no feature code. - I did not run the gate with `--base upstream/main`. On a stacked branch that plan has 916 steps. It tests #2716 and the changes on `main` after the base of #2716, not this commit. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. ## Refresh with main (review of `bd24b9328`) `main` was merged into the branch (merge commits, no rebase). Main took project v73 for `do_not_touch` (#2055). The sketch picks and `chain_overrides` of #1864 now use v74: - `crates/app/src/project/file.rs`: `PROJECT_VERSION` is 74. A v73 reader refuses a file with sketch picks. - A v73 file steps up to v74 and keeps its `do_not_touch` protection. - `SetOperationGeometry` keeps the per-chain override seat and main's `do_not_touch` overlap refusal. Main's new code matches `FeatureSel` exhaustively. title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |
| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |
| motion: the allowance grows the material (`Guards::allowance`) | same | red |
| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 3914606bf: green, 359 steps, 0 failed (55.5 min). The diff against `upstream/main` holds #2822 too, so its suites ran. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat base-2822 HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.
The diff against `upstream/main` shows 3 deleted `.nc` files under `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/`. The base (#2822, head 8040ea771) does not have them yet. This PR does not touch them. A merge of main brings them back.

## Not exercised

- The rows of the group on the 2D Adaptive page. The page keeps the value of the draft and shows no rows. Follow-up: #2884.
- The MCP skill row. The session could not write `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. Follow-up, with the row text: #2885.
- A golden CL file for the rest pass of the 2D Adaptive. The tests read the path against a simulation.
- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup, a WCS yaw, and the field stock engine. The code path is that of #2822, which has the same limits.
- Islands and a neck in the app job. The motion suite of #2031 covers them on a proved stock, not on the column stock.
- Stock to leave on this operation together with the group.
- The toolpath on a machine.
- Linux only; debug build. The app was not started by hand.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/1446-rest-adaptive-op.md`)

- Real residue thinner than the film (2.4 cells) along a wall is not cut.
- The `entry` field and the links of the operation are not read with the group on. Each entry is a plunge into proved-clear space.
- #2032 (entry with clearance proved for the full cutter, on the 2D Pocket) stays open and is not part of this PR.

## Literature

- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, Springer, 1991.
- Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta, D. S. Nau, "Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems", Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The stock-proof rules are the decision of this project. No code or text of a different CAM product was read or used.

## Overlaps

- #2822 (base of this stack): `rest_op.rs` (`rest_of`, `rest_refusal`, `reads_previous_ops`), `job.rs` (the previous-operations arm), `params.rs`, `generate.rs`.
- #2842 changes the level ladder lines in `adaptive::rest::guarded`. This PR moves those two lines into `adaptive::rest_levels`. It is the same code. The PR that merges second applies the step of #2842 in `rest_levels`.
- #2833 and #2831 add fields to the pocket family. They touch the same constructor lists of `OpParams::Adaptive2D` (the kinds seed, the project mapping, seven test files). Each side adds lines. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2853, #2817, #2836, #2716, #2714, #2678 touch the same files in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive operation has rest machining from the previous operations: it cuts only what the earlier operations of the setup left, and each plunge stands where their stock proves the cutter clear (set through MCP or the project file; the page rows follow in #2884).

Effort: max

Fixes #1446

The production fix is already on main in `bc5daa32d` (`outer_fills`).
The remaining diff adds the chord-bore test and `docs/decisions/2849-corner-cusp-loop.md`.
Main's bow-tie test checks `outer_fills` directly. This test covers both corner-check entry points.

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
Stacked on #2714 (merge #2714 first)

## What changed

This fix changes 23 files relative to parent `b95c27b2e`.
It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.
The images are stored only on `mkinney/Camcraft` branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`:

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.
The correct finish electrode then failed the extent check.
The original pin reported a burned X extent of `19.962` for a `20.000` cavity.

## Tests

The original pin failed before the production change:

- `a_diamond_cavity_finish_is_generated_and_judged_clean`

The MCP pin covers schema discovery, translated outlines, generation, null clearing and early refusals:

- `mcp_exposes_the_cavity_outline_and_burns_a_diamond_finish`

The ten motion pins pass:

- `a_diamond_finish_is_judged_on_wall_offsets`
- `matching_extents_do_not_hide_an_oversized_electrode_outline`
- `a_finish_that_leaves_a_wall_undersize_is_refused`
- `malformed_cavity_outlines_are_refused_by_name`
- `an_excessive_cavity_outline_is_refused_before_geometry`
- `a_cavity_outline_that_collapses_on_the_geometry_lattice_is_refused`
- `cavity_outline_extents_must_match_the_stated_size`
- `an_undersize_that_consumes_the_cavity_is_refused`
- `a_small_electrode_cannot_hide_a_gap_that_burns_past_the_floor`
- `a_vector_orbit_does_not_certify_angled_walls`

Each mutation failed its pin with the old code or the guard removed.
Each pin passed after restoration:

- `old-generator`: red / green.
- `shape-point-limit`: red / green.
- `region-lattice`: red / green.
- `extentmatch`: red / green.
- `consumed-inset`: red / green.
- `scalar-floor`: red / green.
- `vector`: red / green.
- `containment`: red / green.
- `finish-coverage`: red / green.
- `early-shape`: red / green.
- `missing-electrode`: red / green.
- `early-size`: red / green.

Final targeted runs passed 11 app tests and 10 motion tests.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 780 steps.
It passed 779 steps and found one failure in the rectangular MCP reply.
The reply now uses `null` for the absent outline.
The failed step passed on rerun.
All three affected app binaries then passed.
The final early-size guard also passed its red/green check.
Clippy passed for all five touched crates with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
Formatting checks passed for the three new Rust files.

## Goldens moved

This fix changes no `.nc` or `.cl` files relative to `base-2714`.
The required comparison with `upstream/main` shows 13 inherited differences.
Each complete file diff was checked.

Parent commit `b95c27b2e` adds these four files:

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_slot_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

- `face_contour_and_slot_take_arc_turns_and_a_radius_through_edit_operation_and_undo`
- `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key`
- `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`
- `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp`

Two unit tests in `blend.rs`: `a_user_radius_turns_on_corner_arcs_where_the_stride_has_room` and `a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` (review fix). Two unit tests there changed with the plan type (`bool` became `Option<Turn>`).

Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the motion pin does not compile, because `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` and `SlotParams` have no such fields (`error[E0560]`).

Mutation results. Each mutation put one guard back to the old behaviour. Each pin went red, and green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Contour reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Contour has no radius door | `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Face does not read `blend_radius` | `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Face has no radius door | `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off` | red |
| Face step goes inside the overrun line | `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line` | red |
| Face corner arcs only for rows within the tool diameter | `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool` | red |
| Slot rounds nothing | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot has no radius door | `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Slot reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot of one row says nothing | `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so` | red |
| `sane.rs` door without the three kinds | `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Face radius | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Slot option | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Contour radius | `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| Slot digest without the option | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Face digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Contour digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Slot project file drops the option on save | `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key` | red |
| Face takes the semicircle when half the spacing is less than 0.005 mm past the radius (review fix) | `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short`, `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` | red (`actual radii: [0.012500000000000178]` for 0.01 mm) |

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

Pins: `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (the reviewer's 60 x 10.025 mm case and three other spacings), and the unit test `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius`.

### Review fix: the exhaustive test literals

The latest review found missing required fields in nine exhaustive test literals from main. The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`.

- Face literals have `blend_radius: None` in `chamfer_partly_bevelled`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `setup_move_order`, `stock_copy_hole`, `vouch_fidelity` and `vouch_fidelity_mcp`.
- Slot literals have `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in `tilt_basis0_edited_file` and `tilt_stock_cap`.
- Current main adds the same missing Face default in `first_traverse_mill_turn` and `model_fidelity_wide`. These literals have `blend_radius: None` too.

- Current main also adds a Contour literal and a Slot literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`. The Contour literal has `blend_radius: None`. The Slot literal has `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None`.

- The test helper in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` also has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`.

- The Contour literal in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs` has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `equal_steps::edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`.

The fix adds 18 default-field lines in fourteen files. All changed literals are in tests. It changes no runtime source logic.

Runtime pins: eleven app suites passed 47 tests. Motion `equal_steps` passed 13 tests. The app first-traverse unit pin passed one test. App `equal_steps` passed six tests.

Mutation: removing the added defaults gave compiler error `E0063` in the affected literals. Restoring the defaults made all fourteen affected suites compile and pass.

Final head: `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`

Quick gate: 761 steps passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`, against upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`. The first run passed all 123 motion steps. The app build then stopped on a stale local `camcraft_kernel` artifact (`E0463`) after the check profile changed. After rebuilding that local artifact, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only app --only ui` passed all 638 selected steps, with 0 failed, in 38.6 minutes. These two runs cover the quick plan: 7,028 tests passed, 0 failed and 115 ignored. No source change was needed for the artifact failure.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`: 237 steps, 0 failed, in 44.3 minutes. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran. The lanes ran 100 passing tests and six expected failures: three for #1950 and three for #2849. There were 0 unexpected failures. Motion had 38 steps and 57 passing tests. App had 198 steps and 43 passing tests. The shared build was one step.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed in 40.41 seconds.

## Screenshots

The images show the Passes tab of the Properties panel, cropped. A temporary test rendered the real egui shell with `Harness::render()`. That test is not in the PR. "Before" is `upstream/main` `5fdbed9bd` with arc turns on. "After" is this PR with arc turns on and a radius set. The header of the panel names the seeded operation, so the crop leaves it out. The images are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

Face, before and after (default, then a 2 mm radius):

![Face before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-before.png)
![Face after, default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-after-default.png)
![Face after, 2 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-after-radius.png)

2D Contour, before and after (1 mm radius):

![Contour before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/contour-before.png)
![Contour after, 1 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/contour-after-radius.png)

Slot, before (no option) and after (1 mm radius):

![Slot before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/slot-before.png)
![Slot after, 1 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/slot-after-radius.png)

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. The default output of each kind did not change.

## Size of the diff

The diff touches about 290 files. Most hunks are one line: an exhaustive `OpParams::Face`, `OpParams::Contour`, `OpParams::Slot`, `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` or `SlotParams` literal gets `blend_radius: None` (and `blend_turns: false` for Slot). The logic is in these files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/blend.rs`, `face.rs`, `slots.rs`, `slot_turns.rs` (new), `contour_params.rs`, `tab_bridge.rs`
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `types/sane.rs`, `generate.rs`, `params.rs`, `params/mill2d.rs`
- `crates/app/src/project/params.rs`, `params_impl.rs`

- No posted G-code test for the new Face corner arcs or the Slot arcs. The post reads them as the same G2/G3 moves that the semicircle and the pocket arcs give.

- 2D Contour generation with a radius ran through the app only as a refusal (a radius past the tool radius). The arcs at the radius are pinned in the motion crate.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

When no earlier operation cut, the stock is known. The whole pocket is cut and a note says it.

## Cause

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

## Tests

Pins, all new:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_tests.rs` (lib): `each_reading_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `a_floor_cut_at_the_cut_depth_does_not_stand_and_one_above_it_does`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_previous.rs`: 6 tests. They compare the rest area with an independent simulation of the earlier operations: a flat tool, a wall allowance, a bull-nose tool, mixed tools with a partial depth and disconnected cuts, an island. The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` now also covers the mode.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/rest_source_tests.rs`: 2 tests for the new row.

Red before the change: the pins use the new API and do not compile on `upstream/main`. Thus the mutation results below are the proof for each guard.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| every cut depth is read (`Guards::depth`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| an unreadable column stands (`Guards::unknown`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| the pocket outside the grid stands (`Guards::outside`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| one cell of growth (`Guards::cell`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| `rest_plan` refuses the new mode | `the_two_rest_modes_never_use_each_others_planner` | red | green |
| `rest_pocket_previous` refuses the entered mode | same | red | green |
| `validate` does not read the previous tool in the new mode | same | red | green |
| job: tilted plane refused | `a_tilted_plane_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_at_generation` | red | green |
| door: tilted plane refused at the edit | same | red | green |
| job: `previous_ops_refusal` is called | `a_stock_that_cannot_be_established_is_refused_by_name` | red | green |
| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |
| earlier operation stale | same | red | green |
| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |
| stamp byte 0xD8 | `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

## Review evidence on the final head

title: feat(ui): stock axis choice on the Stock page (along Z, X, Y or custom)
body:
## What changed

- The Stock page has a "Stock axis" choice: Along Z (default), Along X, Along Y and Custom. Custom shows three angles in degrees: turn about Z (yaw), tilt about Y (pitch), tilt about X (roll). The choice applies to a box and to a cylinder. The old "Rotation (yaw deg)" row is replaced.
- The turn is stored in the stock's existing `Location.rot`. There is no new shape field and no project-file version step.
- Apply sends the whole turn through the undoable `SetStock` (new UI queue entry `CommandKind::SetStockPose`; the old `CommandKind::SetStock { yaw_deg }` stays for its callers). Undo restores the old turn.
- The page reads a stored turn back. A preset turn shows its preset. Any other turn shows Custom with its angles (`camcraft_geometry::geometry::stock_axis`).
- Before any simulation, the page shows a plain note when the simulation cannot cut the drafted stock: a stock tilted off the axes. Since #2758 the simulation cuts a cylinder laid along X or Y. The note asks the simulation's own law (`stock_follow::sim_frame`). The refusals `OBLIQUE_STOCK` and `LAID_CYLINDER` do not change. A box laid along X or Y is a square turn, so the simulation cuts it and no note shows.
- MCP `set_stock` takes an optional `axis` ("z", "x", "y") or `angles_deg` ({yaw, pitch, roll}), not both. It calls the same `SetStock` and returns `{ stock, axis, angles_deg }`. The camcraft-mcp skill row is updated.
- `sketch.rs`: the DXF profile face ignored the stock's turn. Now an upright stock keeps its top face, a stock laid square is read as the same solid unturned, and a laid cylinder or a tilted stock is refused by name (`sketch::NO_TOP_FACE`). `ImportDxf` shows that refusal.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2576-stock-axis.md`.
- Follow-up: #2758 (stock simulation: cut a cylinder or box stock that lies along X or Y).

Process change: yes

## Readings

- X preset = a quarter turn about Y (stock Z goes to world +X). Y preset = a minus quarter turn about X (stock Z goes to world +Y).
- A laid 50 x 40 x 20 box at (3, 4, 5): the profile face is at the highest Z of the turned box, and its normal is world +Z (pinned).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `set_stock_lays_a_cylinder_along_x_and_undo_restores_the_old_turn`
  - `a_turned_stock_survives_the_project_file`
  - `mcp_set_stock_takes_an_axis_and_undo_walks_it_back`
  - `a_profile_lies_on_a_laid_box_and_a_laid_cylinder_is_refused`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `the_stock_page_offers_the_stock_axis_and_custom_angles`
  - `apply_lays_the_stock_along_x_and_undo_stands_it_up_again`
  - `a_custom_turn_reads_back_with_its_angles`
  - `a_laid_stock_shows_no_simulation_note_and_a_tilted_one_does`
- `fit_to_models_wraps_the_part_in_a_laid_stocks_frame` (Fit to Models on a laid stock fits in the frame of the stock)
- `layout_page_stock` now has the "Stock axis" anchor.
- `camcraft-geometry` unit tests: `each_preset_carries_the_stock_axis_onto_its_world_axis`, `custom_angles_read_back_and_a_bad_angle_is_refused`.
- The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 4. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Gate

The gate is on ee65e8666. The PR comment of the review fix has the details.
- Quick gate on b44e15628: 1038 steps. The 2 red steps (`stock_axis`, `mcp_doc_drift`) came from main (#2758 and the tool reference doc). Both are fixed in ee65e8666, and those suites and the sketch suites pass there.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: 1388 passed, 0 failed.
- Clippy `-D warnings` on `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: 234 reached (197 app, 37 motion). Not run. The cut gate covers them.
- New pinning test: `fit_to_models_wraps_the_part_in_a_laid_stocks_frame`.

## Screenshots

The pictures are renders of the real shell through the egui_kittest renderer (the same frame code), with the seeded test document and a 40 x 100 cylinder. They are not captures of a live app window.

Before (main):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2576/stock-before.png)

title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins cover the new behaviour. Each review fix below also has a direct test and mutation check.

- `camcraft-tools --lib` (`107 passed; 0 failed`): `undercut::tests` checks sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, and the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (`459 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`): `machining2d::undercut::tests` pins single-station Z moves, entry slot refusals, concentric arc slots, profile contact offsets, and input refusals.
- `camcraft-sim --test undercut_laws` (`14 passed; 0 failed`): pins `UndercutLift`, `ShankHit`, `acquit_undercut_by_prior`, `Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`, `Atom::cap`, and `Stock::simulate_undercut`.
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_slot_undercut` (`7 passed; 0 failed`): pins MCP cutting, verification, posting, refusals, `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts`, and `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play` (`8 passed; 0 failed`): pins `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play_partial` (`4 passed; 0 failed`): pins `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy`.
- `camcraft-motion --test golden_undercut`: pins four golden CL files. The generator suite and its unchanged goldens now live in `crates/motion/tests/`.
- `camcraft-app --test tool_law` (`5 passed; 0 failed`): pins undercut cutter compatibility.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` (`1256 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`): includes `tool_undercut_row::tests`, `tool_cutter_params::each_milling_kind_shows_the_parameters_its_outline_is_drawn_from`, and `tests/tool_undercut.rs` (`new_tool_undercut_kinds_seed_sane_defaults_hide_corner_radius_and_show_dovetail_flank_angle`, `dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_without_corner_radius`, and `slot_undercut_page_shows_its_geometry_heights_passes_and_feeds_fields`).

Review-fix mutation checks (guard reverted -> RED, restored -> GREEN):

- UI dovetail flank angle, undercut defaults, and corner-radius filter reverted: RED (`3 failed` across `tests/tool_undercut.rs` and `tool_cutter_params`). Restored: GREEN (`11 passed; 0 failed`).
